好吃.etymology: Evaluative compound adjective combining 好 ('good to…, pleasant to…', read hǎo) + 吃 ('eat'): 'good to eat -> delicious, tasty'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好吃 (via 萌典)

好听.etymology: Evaluative compound adjective combining 好 ('pleasant to…') + 听 (聽, 'listen to, hear'): 'pleasant to listen to -> nice-sounding, melodious, pleasing to the ear'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好听 (via 萌典)

好喝.etymology: Evaluative compound adjective combining 好 ('pleasant to…') + 喝 ('drink'): 'good to drink -> tasty, delicious (of beverages or soup)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好喝 (via 萌典)

好在.etymology: Modal adverb and verb phrase combining 好 ('what is good/fortunate is…') + 在 ('lie in, consist in'): literally 'the good thing lies in…' -> 'fortunately, luckily, thank goodness that'.

history.meaning: the good thing is that -> fortunately, luckily

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好在 (via 萌典)

好奇.etymology: Verb-object compound used as an adjective, combining 好 (here read hào in the fourth tone, the Classical verb meaning 'be fond of, love') + 奇 ('novelty, strange or unfamiliar things'): 'curious, inquisitive'. Attested since Han historical prose (e.g., Sima Qian's Shiji).

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese (Shiji, Hanshu) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: fond of the novel/unusual -> curious, inquisitive

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好奇 (via 萌典)

好好.etymology: Reduplication of 好 ('good, well', read hǎohǎo or hǎohāor in northern speech): functions as an adverb meaning 'properly, carefully, thoroughly, to one's heart's content' (好好休息 'get a good rest') and as an adjective meaning 'perfectly fine, in good condition'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好好 (via 萌典)

好看.etymology: Evaluative compound adjective combining 好 ('pleasant to…') + 看 ('look at, watch'): 'pleasing to the eye -> good-looking, pretty, attractive; interesting (of a book, play, or film)'.

history.meaning: pleasing to look at; pretty; good-looking; interesting

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好看 (via 萌典)

好让.etymology: Purposive conjunction combining modal/purposive 好 ('so as to, so that it is easy to…') + causative verb 让 (讓, 'let, allow'): 'so as to let, in order that'.

history.meaning: so as to let; so that

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好让 (via 萌典)

好运.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 好 ('good') + 运 (運, 'revolving fortune, luck'): 'good luck, good fortune'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好运 (via 萌典)

如果.etymology: Conditional conjunction combining two Classical conditional markers: 如 ('if, suppose') + 果 ('if indeed, really, as expected'): 'if, in case, supposing that'. Attested from Tang–Song poetry and prose.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 如果 (via 萌典)

妈妈.etymology: Intimate reduplication of 妈 (woman classifier 女 + phonetic 马 mǎ), part of the near-universal bilabial nasal nursery pattern for 'mother' while anchored in Chinese script since the Guangyun dictionary (Middle Chinese).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 妈妈 (via 萌典)

妙.etymology: Ideographic/phono-semantic character combining 女 ('woman/maiden') + 少 ('young/subtle', also written 玅 with 玄 'mysterious'): in Classical Chinese (Laozi's 众妙之门) 'subtle, mysterious, wondrous', and in everyday Mandarin 'wonderful, clever, ingenious, fine'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 妙 (via 萌典)

姑姑.etymology: Affectionate kinship reduplication of 姑 (woman classifier 女 + phonetic 古 gǔ), attested since the Erya and Book of Odes specifically for one's father's sister—reflecting Chinese kinship's precise distinction between paternal (姑姑) and maternal (姨妈/阿姨) aunts.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 姑姑 (via 萌典)

姑娘.etymology: Compound noun combining 姑 ('father's sister; young unmarried woman') + 娘 ('mother; young woman', neutral tone niang in this word): 'unmarried young woman, girl; daughter; (historically) paternal aunt'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 姑娘 (via 萌典)

姓.etymology: Ancient ideogram/phono-semantic character attested on Shang oracle bones combining 女 ('woman') + 生 ('be born, give birth'): originally denoted a matriarchal clan lineage name shared by those born of the same ancestral mother (such as the ancient 姬, 姜, 嬴, 姒 clan names containing 女), now the general noun and verb for 'family name, surname; be surnamed'.

history.meaning: born of the same clan mother = ancestral clan surname

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 姓 (via 萌典)

嫩.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 女 ('delicate') + 敕 (shù/nèn): 'tender, soft, delicate (of young shoots, meat, or skin); inexperienced; light/pale (of colors)'.

history.stage: Classical & Medieval Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 嫩 (via 萌典)

字.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on bronze vessels showing a child (子) under a house roof (宀): originally 'give birth to, rear and nurture a child' (and 'a woman's betrothal', 待字闺中). Because characters proliferated by compounding radicals and phonetics like offspring, since the Qin dynasty 字 has meant 'written Chinese character, word, script, handwriting' (as well as an adult courtesy name).

history.meaning: child under a roof = bear/rear offspring; adult courtesy name

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 字 (via 萌典)

字母.etymology: Compound noun of 字 ('written word/character') + 母 ('mother, generative root'). Originally coined by Tang–Song Chinese phonologists (after Buddhist Sanskrit models) for the 36 initial consonant exemplars (三十六字母) from which syllables were generated, and adopted in modern Mandarin for an 'alphabetic letter, alphabet'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 字母 (via 萌典)

字迹.etymology: Compound noun of 字 ('written characters') + 迹 (跡, 'footprints, traces, marks'): 'handwriting, written characters/script left on a surface'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 字迹 (via 萌典)

孙子.etymology: Kinship noun formed from 孙 (孫, combining 子 'child' + 系 'thread of descent/continuation': 'child's child, descendant') + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): 'grandson (specifically son's son)' (contrast классический 孫子 Sūnzǐ with full third tone on 子, 'Master Sun', author of The Art of War).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 孙子 (via 萌典)

学校.etymology: Coordinative noun compound pairing two ancient Zhou-era educational institutions mentioned in Mencius (设痒序学校以教之): 学 (學, 'institution of higher learning; study') + 校 (xiào, 'community school and military training enclosure'). Standardized across modern East Asia for any 'school, educational institution'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 学校 (via 萌典)

孩子.etymology: Compound noun of 孩 ('laughing infant, young child', from 子 'child' + phonetic 亥 hài, originally 咳 'infant's giggle' in Laozi and Mencius) + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): 'child, kid; one's son or daughter'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 孩子 (via 萌典)

宁静.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 宁 (寧, 'peaceful, settled at heart under a roof with a dish of food') + 静 (靜, 'quiet, still, calm'): 'peaceful and quiet, tranquil, serene'. Famously in Zhuge Liang's 夫君子之行，静以修身…非淡泊无以明志，非宁静无以致远.

history.stage: Classical Chinese (Chuci, Huainanzi, Zhuge Liang) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 宁静 (via 萌典)

它.etymology: Non-human third-person singular pronoun ('it'). In Shang oracle-bone script, 它 was the original pictograph of a cobra/snake (written 蛇 shé after the insect/reptile radical 虫 was added), borrowed in Classical Chinese to mean 'other, another' (later written 他 with 亻). During the early 20th-century vernacular movement, 它 (alongside 牠 for animals) was standardized with the pronunciation tā for inanimate 'it', contrasting graphically with 他 ('he') and 她 ('she').

morphemes.meaning: classical 'other' standardized in modern Chinese for inanimate 'it' (tā)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 它 (via 萌典)

它们.etymology: Non-human third-person plural pronoun ('they, them [for things, plants, and animals]'), formed by adding the plural suffix 们 (-men) to the inanimate pronoun 它 ('it').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 它们 (via 萌典)

守.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on bronze inscriptions combining 宀 ('roof, building, court') + 寸 ('hand; law/measure'): 'guard, defend, keep watch over, abide by (rules/promises), stay close by'.

history.meaning: guard a territory/post; abide by; keep
guard; defend; observe/abide by; stay close to

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 守 (via 萌典)

安全.etymology: Coordinative adjective and noun compound of 安 ('peaceful, settled, safe', a woman 女 settled indoors under a roof 宀) + 全 ('whole, intact, unharmed'): 'safe and sound, secure; safety, security'. Attested since Classical prose (Xunzi, Hanshu).

history.stage: Classical Chinese (Xunzi, Hanshu) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 安全 (via 萌典)

安排.etymology: Coordinative verb and noun compound of 安 ('settle, place securely') + 排 ('set in order, line up'): 'arrange, plan, set up, schedule; arrangement'. First attested in Zhuangzi and popularized from Tang–Song poetry and vernacular onward.

history.meaning: settle and put in order -> arrange, plan, schedule

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 安排 (via 萌典)

安静.etymology: Coordinative adjective and verb compound of 安 ('peaceful, settled, calm', woman 女 under a roof 宀) + 静 (靜, 'quiet, still, free of noise'): 'quiet, peaceful, calm; quiet down'. Attested since Classical prose (Xunzi, Shiji).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 安静 (via 萌典)

宋.etymology: Ancient character combining 宀 ('roof, ancestral temple') + 木 ('tree/wood'): originally the name of the Zhou-era feudal state of Song (founded in eastern Henan by descendants of the Shang royal house), later the prestigious Song Dynasty (960–1279 CE), and a major Chinese surname.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Bronze inscriptions & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: State of Song; Song Dynasty; surname Song

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 宋 (via 萌典)

完.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 宀 ('roof, house') + 元 (yuán/wán phonetic, 'head/primary'): originally 'an intact, completed building without damage', hence 'whole, intact, complete; finish, run out of, come to an end' and Mandarin's primary completive verb complement (-wán).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 完 (via 萌典)

完了.etymology: Verb/adjective + aspectual/modal particle 了 (le) from 完 ('finish, come to an end'): means literally 'be finished / done / over', and as a colloquial exclamation 'it's all over!, we're done for!, uh-oh!'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 完了 (via 萌典)

完全.etymology: Coordinative adjective and adverb compound of 完 ('intact, complete') + 全 ('whole, entire'): 'complete, whole; completely, entirely, totally'. Attested since Han historical prose (Shiji).

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese (Shiji) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 完全 (via 萌典)

完好.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 完 ('intact, undamaged') + 好 ('good, sound'): 'intact, in good condition, undamaged'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 完好 (via 萌典)

完好无损.etymology: Four-character idiom combining 完好 ('intact and in good condition') + 无损 ('without damage or loss', 无 'without' + 损 'damage'): 'completely intact and undamaged, in mint/unscathed condition'.

history.form: 完好無損 / 完好无损
history.meaning: completely intact without the slightest damage

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 完好无损 (via 萌典)

完整.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 完 ('whole, intact') + 整 ('orderly, whole, complete'): 'complete, intact, integrated, undivided'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 完整 (via 萌典)

完美.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 完 ('complete, flawless') + 美 ('beautiful, fine, admirable'): 'perfect, flawless, consummate'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 完美 (via 萌典)

定.etymology: Ancient ideogram combining 宀 ('roof, house') + 正 ('upright; foot 止 settled at a line'): 'settle down indoors -> fix, settle, decide, calm, book/reserve/order in advance, surely'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 定 (via 萌典)

定好.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining 定 ('decide, fix, arrange') + 好 (resultative complement of satisfactory completion): 'settle upon, agree on, fix (a date, plan, or price) satisfactorily'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 定好 (via 萌典)

实在.etymology: Compound of 实 (實, 'real, solid, true') + 在 ('exist, be present'). Functions both as an adjective ('honest, dependable, solid, real') and as an adverb ('really, truly, honestly, indeed').

history.stage: Tang–Song Buddhist & vernacular Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 实在 (via 萌典)

实情.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 实 (實, 'true, actual') + 情 ('situation, facts, circumstances'): 'the true situation, the actual facts, the truth of the matter'.

history.meaning: the actual facts; the truth of a matter

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 实情 (via 萌典)

实话.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 实 (實, 'true, honest') + 话 (話, 'spoken words'): 'truth, honest words'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 实话 (via 萌典)

实话实说.etymology: Four-character idiomatic phrase built on the repetition of 实 ('true, honestly'): 实话 ('true words') + 实说 ('speak frankly/truthfully') = 'tell the plain truth, speak frankly and honestly'.

history.form: 實話實說 / 实话实说
history.meaning: speak the plain truth; be completely frank

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 实话实说 (via 萌典)

客人.etymology: Compound noun of 客 ('guest, visitor, traveler', roof 宀 + 各 'arrive at a lodging') + 人 ('person'): 'guest, visitor, customer/client'. Attested since Han–Tang poetry and prose.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 客人 (via 萌典)

客房.etymology: Compound noun of 客 ('guest') + 房 ('room'): 'guest room (in a house or hotel)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 客房 (via 萌典)

客栈.etymology: Traditional courtyard inn or boutique guesthouse (counted with 家: 一家客栈), combining 客 ('traveler, guest') with 栈 ('wooden gallery, storehouse, wayside lodge'). Historic 客棧 served merchants and travelers along imperial post roads and remain iconic in preserved old quarters of Chengdu and Southwest China.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 客棧 (via 萌典)

客气.etymology: Compound noun, adjective, and verb of 客 ('guest') + 气 (氣, 'manner, air, demeanor', neutral tone qi in this word): literally 'the polite, deferential manner of a guest', hence 'polite, courteous, modest; stand on ceremony (别客气 don't be polite / you're welcome)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 客气 (via 萌典)

家.etymology: Ancient character attested on Shang oracle bones showing a pig/boar (豕) beneath a roof (宀)—as domestic pig-rearing and ancestral offerings under a roof defined a settled household: 'home, family, household; specialist (-ist, as in 画家, 作家); classifier for families, shops, or companies'.

history.meaning: roof over a domesticated pig = household, family, home
home; family; specialist suffix; classifier for businesses/households

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 家 (via 萌典)

家人.etymology: Compound noun of 家 ('family, household') + 人 ('person, members'): 'family members, one's family, household'. Attested since the Yijing (Hexagram 37 家人) and Mencius.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese (Yijing, Mencius) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 家人 (via 萌典)

家具.etymology: Compound noun of 家 ('home, household') + 具 ('utensils, implements, furnishings', originally two hands holding a vessel/shell): 'household furniture'. Attested from Tang–Song texts onward.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 家具 (via 萌典)

家里.etymology: Locative compound combining 家 ('home, family') + 里 (裡, 'inside', neutral tone li): 'at home, in the family, home'.

history.meaning: at home; inside the house; one's family

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 家里 (via 萌典)

容易.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 容 ('allow, accommodate, leisurely') + 易 (yì, 'easy, effortless'). Attested since Han texts (such as Dongfang Shuo's 谈何容易 'how could it be so easy to speak of?').

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 容易 (via 萌典)

宽.etymology: Phono-semantic/ideographic character (traditional 寬, combining roof 宀 + 萈 huán, a wild goat with wide-curving horns): 'wide, broad (opposite of 窄 'narrow'); spacious; lenient, relax/relieve (宽心)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 宽 (via 萌典)

宽度.etymology: Abstract measurement noun combining 宽 ('wide, broad') + 度 ('measure, degree, dimension'): 'width, breadth'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 宽度 (via 萌典)

寄.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 宀 ('house, lodging') + 奇 (qí/jì phonetic): originally 'lodge temporarily at another's house, entrust to someone's care', and by extension 'send, mail, post (letters or parcels); depend on'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 寄 (via 萌典)

对.etymology: Originally 對 (showing a hand 寸 holding a lush upright stand/chisel 丵): in Classical Chinese 'respond/reply to a superior, face toward, match as a pair'. In Mandarin it means 'correct, right!; pair/couple (classifier); treat/face; preposition toward/to'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 对 (via 萌典)

对不起.etymology: Sincere everyday apology ('I'm sorry'), a potential-complement phrase literally meaning 'unable to face (you) squarely / let you down': 对 ('face, treat rightly') + 不 ('not') + 起 ('measure up'). Standardized in Qing and modern Mandarin alongside its classic reassuring reply 没关系 ('it doesn't matter').

history.meaning: have let someone down; 'I am sorry'

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 對不起 (via 萌典)

对面.etymology: Locative and relational noun combining 对 ('face directly across') + 面 ('face, side'): 'opposite, across from, right in front, the other side'.

history.stage: Tang–Song poetry & vernacular to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: face-to-face; across the way; opposite side

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 对面 (via 萌典)

封.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on Shang oracle bones showing a hand/measure (寸) planting trees (丰/木) on an earthen mound (土) to mark a fief boundary: 'enfeoff, confer a title; seal up, close securely; envelope' and the standard classifier for letters (一封信).

history.meaning: mound with boundary trees = fief, boundary, seal up
seal; close; envelope; classifier for letters

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 封 (via 萌典)

将.etymology: Phono-semantic character (將, combining 爿 qiáng phonetic + 肉/夕 'meat' + 寸 'hand'): originally 'take/offer meat in hand -> escort, support, lead'. Read jiāng as an adverb ('be about to, will soon'), pre-verbal disposal/instrument marker (like 把), and verb ('take'); read jiàng as 'military general; check in chess'.

history.meaning: escort, hold, about to (jiāng); military commander (jiàng)
will/about to; formal disposal preposition (jiāng); general (jiàng)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 将 (via 萌典)

小.etymology: Ancient indicative/pictographic character attested on Shang oracle bones written with three tiny dots or grains of sand (小): 'small, little, young, minor, brief' and an affectionate/humble prefix before names or kinship terms (小晴, 小张).

morphemes.meaning: three small dots = small, little, young

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: three tiny specks = small, little, young

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 小 (via 萌典)

小心.etymology: Compound verb and adjective of 小 ('make small, cautious,細緻') + 心 ('heart, mind'). In the Shijing (小心翼翼), 小心 meant 'reverent, circumspect, and scrupulously attentive in heart'; in everyday Mandarin it means 'be careful, watch out!, cautious'.

history.meaning: reverent and scrupulously cautious in mind

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 小心 (via 萌典)

小时.etymology: Compound time noun of 小 ('small, halved') + 时 (時, 'traditional double-hour 时辰'). Because the traditional Chinese day was divided into 12 时辰 (each equal to two modern hours), when the Western 24-hour clock was adopted in late Qing China, each 60-minute unit (half of a 大时/时辰) was named 小时 ('small hour' = 'hour').

history.meaning: half of a traditional two-hour 时辰 = 60-minute hour

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 小时 (via 萌典)

小时候.etymology: Three-character temporal noun phrase combining 小 ('young, little in age') + 时候 ('time, period'): 'in one's childhood, when one was little/young'.

history.meaning: when one was young; in childhood

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 小时候 (via 萌典)

小晴.etymology: Affectionate/familiar personal name formed with the endearing prefix 小 ('little, young', placed before a given name or surname among friends, family, and coworkers) + given name 晴 ('clear, sunny sky').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 小晴 (via 萌典)

小美.etymology: Affectionate/familiar personal name formed with the endearing prefix 小 ('little, young') + given name 美 ('beautiful, fine'): 'Xiaomei'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 小美 (via 萌典)

小节.etymology: Compound noun of 小 ('small, minor') + 节 (節, 'bamboo node, section, division'). In Classical prose it meant 'minor details of conduct or etiquette' (不拘小节); in modern music it is the standard term for a 'musical measure, bar'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 小节 (via 萌典)

小路.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 小 ('small, narrow') + 路 ('road, path'): 'narrow path, lane, trail, footpath'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 小路 (via 萌典)

小院.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 小 ('small, cozy') + 院 ('walled courtyard, compound'): 'small courtyard'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 小院 (via 萌典)

小院客栈.etymology: Four-character compound combining 小院 ('small courtyard') + 客栈 ('traditional inn, guesthouse', 客 'traveler/guest' + 栈 'wooden lodge/storehouse'): 'Courtyard Inn, small courtyard guesthouse'.

history.form: 小院客棧 / 小院客栈

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 小院客栈 (via 萌典)

小鸟.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 小 ('small, little') + 鸟 (鳥, 'bird', a pictograph of a Perched bird with feathers and claws): 'little bird, small bird'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 小鸟 (via 萌典)

尝.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 嘗, combining 尚 shàng/cháng phonetic + 旨 'delicious taste/spoon and sweet mouth'): originally 'taste food, sample a flavor; autumn harvest sacrifice', and in Classical Chinese an experiential past adverb ('once, formerly'); in Mandarin, 'taste, try the flavor of, experience'.

history.meaning: taste food; autumn offering; once in the past

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 尝 (via 萌典)

尝尝.etymology: Reduplicated verb from 尝 ('taste, try the flavor of'): 'have a taste, try a bite' (verb reduplication indicates a light, inviting, or brief sampling action).

history.meaning: have a taste; sample a little

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 尝尝 (via 萌典)

就.etymology: Ideogram combining 京 ('high mound/tower in the capital') + 尤 ('outstanding/reach'): originally 'move toward a high place, approach, take up (a post), accomplish'. In vernacular Mandarin it became one of the language's core adverbs and connectives: 'then, right away, as early as, precisely/just, even if'.

history.meaning: go toward; approach; accomplish; take office

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 就 (via 萌典)

就像.etymology: Simile verb/preposition compound combining emphatic adverb 就 ('just, right, exactly') + 像 ('resemble, be like'): 'just like, exactly as if'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 就像 (via 萌典)

就是.etymology: Emphatic compound combining 就 ('precisely, just') + 是 ('be; right'): functions as an emphatic affirmation ('that's right!, precisely!'), a restrictive focus marker ('only, simply'), and a concessive/adversative connector ('even if; except that').

history.meaning: precisely is; that's right; simply; even if

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 就是 (via 萌典)

就算.etymology: Concessive conjunction combining 就 ('even if') + 算 ('count as, reckon, suppose'): 'even if, granted that, even supposing' (typically paired with 也 in the main clause: 就算…也…).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 就算 (via 萌典)

尺寸.etymology: Coordinative noun compound pairing two traditional Chinese length units: 尺 ('Chinese foot', originally a hand span from thumb to forefinger below 尸, equal to 10 寸) + 寸 ('Chinese inch', a mark 一 one inch below the wrist on a hand 又, where the pulse is felt). Together they mean 'dimensions, measurements, size' (and figuratively 'proper measure/tact', read chǐcun).

history.stage: Classical Chinese (Guanzi, Hanshu) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: feet and inches -> dimensions, size, measurements

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 尺寸 (via 萌典)

尽管.etymology: Compound of 尽 (儘, jǐn, 'to the utmost, freely let') + 管 ('attend to, concern oneself with'). Functions both as a permissive adverb before verbs ('feel free to…, go right ahead without hesitation') and as a concessive conjunction ('even though, despite, although').

history.meaning: feel free to (adverb); despite, even though (conjunction)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 尽管 (via 萌典)

层.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 層, combining 尸 'house/roof' + 曾 céng 'tiered steamer pot, add upon'): 'story, floor (of a building); layer, tier, stratum, level'.

history.meaning: floor/story; layer; tier; classifier for levels

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 层 (via 萌典)

屋子.etymology: Colloquial noun formed from 屋 ('house, room, roof', combining 尸 'roof/shelter' + 至 'where people arrive and rest') + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): 'room; house'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 屋子 (via 萌典)

屋里.etymology: Locative compound combining 屋 ('room, house') + 里 (裡, 'inside'): 'inside the room, indoors, in the house'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 屋里 (via 萌典)

屋顶.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 屋 ('house') + 顶 (頂, 'crown of the head, top'): 'roof, housetop'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 屋顶 (via 萌典)

屏幕.etymology: Coordinative noun compound of 屏 ('folding or standing screen that shields a view', 尸 + 并) + 幕 ('hanging tent or curtain cloth', 莫 + 巾). Originally named traditional decorative screens and stage curtains, then standardized in modern Chinese for a television, computer, phone, or cinema 'screen'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 屏幕 (via 萌典)

山.etymology: Foundational pictograph (象形字) attested from Shang oracle bones depicting three mountain peaks rising side by side: 'mountain, hill, peak'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 山 (via 萌典)

山丘.etymology: Compound noun of 山 ('mountain, hill') + 丘 ('earthen hillock, mound', originally two peaks standing on the ground 一): 'hill, hillock, knoll'. Attested since the Shijing and Chuci.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese (Shijing, Chuci) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 山丘 (via 萌典)

山毛榉木.etymology: Four-character botanical timber compound combining 山毛榉 ('beech tree, Fagus', literally 'mountain hairy zelkova-like tree', named for its hairy leaf margins and triangular nuts) + 木 ('wood, timber'): 'beechwood'.

history.form: 山毛櫸木 / 山毛榉木
history.meaning: beechwood (timber of the Fagus beech tree)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 山毛榉木 (via 萌典)

岁.etymology: Ancient character (traditional 歲) combining 步 ('step, planetary march across the sky') + 戌 ('axe', phonetic and graphic). In early Chinese astronomy, 歲 was the planet Jupiter (岁星), whose 12-year orbital cycle through the 12 ecliptic stations marked one 'year' per station; hence 'year (of harvest or time)' and the standard classifier for 'years of age'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 岁 (via 萌典)

工作.etymology: Coordinative verb and noun compound of 工 ('artisan's square/rammer -> craft, labor, work') + 作 ('make, do, toil'). Attested since the Classic of Poetry and Han texts for 'physical labor, craftwork', and standardized in modern Chinese as the universal noun and verb for 'work, job, employment'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 工作 (via 萌典)

工作室.etymology: Three-character compound of 工作 ('work') + 室 ('room'): 'studio, workshop, atelier, small professional office'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 工作室 (via 萌典)

工具房.etymology: Three-character compound of 工具 ('tools, implements', 工 'work/craft' + 具 'utensil') + 房 ('room, shed'): 'tool room, toolshed'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 工具房 (via 萌典)

工具箱.etymology: Three-character compound of 工具 ('tools') + 箱 ('box, chest, case'): 'toolbox, toolkit'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 工具箱 (via 萌典)

左.etymology: Ancient graph attested on Shang oracle bones as 𠂇 (pictograph of a left hand), to which 工 ('carpenter's square / tool', suggesting the left hand holding a tool to assist) was later added to distinguish 'left (side/hand)' (左) from the verb 'assist' (佐, which added 亻).

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: left hand holding a tool = left (opposite of right 右)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 左 (via 萌典)

左头.etymology: Colloquial locative noun combining 左 ('left') + nominal locative suffix 头 (頭, 'side, end'): 'the left side, on the left'.

history.meaning: the left side; on the left

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 左头 (via 萌典)

左手.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 左 ('left') + 手 ('hand'): 'left hand, left-hand side'. Attested since the Shijing and Classics.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 左手 (via 萌典)

左边.etymology: Locative compound noun of 左 ('left') + 边 (邊, 'side'): 'the left side, to the left'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 左边 (via 萌典)

差.etymology: Ancient graph showing grain/hemp stalks of uneven length above a hand/tool (左/工): read chà 'differ, fall short of, lack (five minutes to…), poor/substandard in quality'; read chā 'difference, discrepancy, error'; read chāi 'send on an official errand (出差)'.

history.meaning: uneven; diverge; err; send on an errand
fall short, lack, poor (chà); difference (chā); errand (chāi)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 差 (via 萌典)

差不多.etymology: Idiomatic verb/adjective/adverb phrase combining 差 ('differ by, fall short by') + 不多 ('not much'): literally 'differs by not much' -> 'almost the same, nearly, just about, good enough'.

history.meaning: differ by very little -> almost the same, nearly, just about

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 差不多 (via 萌典)

差评.etymology: Compound noun and verb combining 差 (chà, 'poor, substandard, bad') + 评 (評, 'evaluation, review, rating'): 'negative review, bad rating'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 差评 (via 萌典)

已经.etymology: Temporal aspect adverb combining two Classical completion words: 已 ('stop, finish, already') + 经 (經, 'pass through, experience, already'): 'already'. Attested from the Six Dynasties and Tang period onward.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 已经 (via 萌典)

巷子.etymology: Colloquial noun formed from 巷 (read xiàng, 'narrow street or residential lane between walls', 共 + 邑/巳) + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): 'lane, alley'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 巷子 (via 萌典)

市.etymology: Ancient character attested on bronze inscriptions showing an enclosed ground with a signpost/banner at the top: originally 'walled marketplace where goods are bought and sold' (and verbally 'buy/trade'), extended in modern administration to 'city, municipality'.

morphemes.meaning: market enclosure and banner = market, city

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 市 (via 萌典)

市场.etymology: Compound noun of 市 ('trade, market') + 场 (場, 'open ground, square, venue'): 'marketplace, bazaar, economic market'. Attested since Han–Tang texts.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 市场 (via 萌典)

市政.etymology: Compound noun of 市 ('city, municipality') + 政 ('government administration, public affairs'): 'municipal administration, civic infrastructure and services'.

history.meaning: municipal government; city administration and public works

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 市政 (via 萌典)

市政厅.etymology: Three-character institutional compound combining 市政 ('municipal administration') + 厅 (廳, 'government hall, administrative building'): 'city hall, town hall'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 市政厅 (via 萌典)

市里.etymology: Locative compound combining 市 ('city, municipality') + 里 (裡, 'inside'): 'in the city, downtown; the municipal authorities'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 市里 (via 萌典)

布.etymology: Phono-semantic character combining 父 (fù/bù phonetic, reduced to 𠂇 at the top) + 巾 ('woven cloth'): originally 'woven hemp or ramie cloth' in Classical Chinese (contrasting with 帛 'silk'), and since the Yuan–Ming introduction of cotton, the general word for 'cotton or woven cloth, fabric; spread/declare/arrange (公布, 布置)'.

history.meaning: hemp cloth; ancient spade-shaped coin; spread out

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 布 (via 萌典)

希望.etymology: Coordinative verb and noun compound of 希 ('look forward to, long for, rare') + 望 ('gaze into the distance, look toward, hope', showing a person 臣 standing on earth 壬 gazing at the distant moon 月). Attested since Classical and Tang prose.

history.stage: Classical & Tang Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: gaze forward in expectation -> hope, wish

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 希望 (via 萌典)

带.etymology: Pictograph (traditional 帶) depicting a woven belt or girdle around the waist with hanging sash ornaments above a cloth (巾): originally 'belt, sash, girdle, ribbon, tire, zone/region', and verbally 'wear at the waist -> carry with one, bring, take along, lead, look after'.

history.meaning: waist belt; sash; carry at the waist

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 带 (via 萌典)

带路.etymology: Verb-object compound of 带 ('lead, guide') + 路 ('the way, road'): 'lead the way, act as a guide'.

history.meaning: lead the way; show the way

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 带路 (via 萌典)

帮.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 幫, combining 封/邦 bāng phonetic + 巾/帛 'cloth/shoe upper'): originally 'the side or upper lining of a shoe sewn on to reinforce it', hence metaphorically 'support from the side -> help, assist' and 'group, gang, band, outer leaves of cabbage'.

history.meaning: side lining reinforcing a shoe; edge

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 帮 (via 萌典)

帮忙.etymology: Separable verb-object compound (离合词) of 帮 ('help, assist') + 忙 ('busy work, pressing tasks'): literally 'help with someone's busy work' -> 'help, lend a hand, do a favor' (e.g., 帮个忙 'do a favor').

history.meaning: help with busy tasks; lend a hand

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 帮忙 (via 萌典)

常春藤.etymology: Botanical compound of 常 ('ever, constant') + 春 ('springtime greenness') + 藤 ('climbing vine', grass/plant crown 艹 + 滕), literally 'ever-spring vine' because its leaves stay glossy green through winter.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 常春藤

干.etymology: Simplified character merging three historical words: (1) 乾 (read gān, 'dry, moisture-free, empty, in vain'), (2) 幹 (read gàn, 'tree trunk -> main body, do, work, capable'), and (3) ancient 干 (pictograph of a forked weapon or shield, read gān: 'shield, offend, have to do with').

morphemes.meaning: dry (乾 gān); do, work (幹 gàn); shield/concern (干 gān)

history.form: 乾 (dry, gān) / 幹 (trunk, do, gàn) / 干 (shield, concern, gān)
history.meaning: three distinct classical words merged in simplified script

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 干 (via 萌典)

干净.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 干 (乾, gān, 'dry, free of mud or moisture') + 净 (淨, 'clean, pure, clear', neutral tone jing in everyday speech): 'clean, neat and tidy; completely'.

history.meaning: dry and clean -> clean, neat, spotless

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 干净 (via 萌典)

干木头.etymology: Three-character modifier-head noun phrase combining 干 (乾, gān, 'dry, seasoned') + 木头 ('wood, timber'): 'dry wood, seasoned timber'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 干木头 (via 萌典)

干杯.etymology: Verb-object compound of 干 (乾, gān, 'empty, drain dry') + 杯 ('cup, glass'): literally 'drain the glass dry' -> 'cheers!, bottoms up!, drink a toast'.

history.meaning: drain one's cup = cheers!, bottoms up!

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 干杯 (via 萌典)

干燥.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 干 (乾, gān, 'dry') + 燥 ('parched, arid, dry', fire 火 + 喿): 'dry, arid, lacking moisture'. Attested since the Huainanzi and medical classics.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 干燥 (via 萌典)

干爽.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 干 (乾, gān, 'dry') + 爽 ('refreshing, crisp, clear'): 'dry and refreshing, pleasantly dry and crisp (of weather, air, or clothing)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 干爽 (via 萌典)

干脆.etymology: Compound adjective and adverb of 干 (乾, gān, 'dry, clean-cut') + 脆 ('crisp, brittle, clear-cut'): describes speech or action that is 'straightforward, clean-cut, decisive', and as a modal adverb 'simply, might as well just…'.

history.meaning: clean-cut and straightforward (adj.); simply, might as well (adv.)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 干脆 (via 萌典)

干透.etymology: Resultative verb/adjective compound combining 干 (乾, gān, 'dry') + 透 ('penetrate all the way through, thoroughly'): 'dry all the way through, completely dry'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 干透 (via 萌典)

平.etymology: Ancient character showing breath or water spreading evenly around a balance bar (于 + 八): 'flat, level, even, smooth; calm, peaceful; equal/draw; ordinary; level tone (平声)'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Bronze inscriptions & Classics) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 平 (via 萌典)

平台.etymology: Compound noun of 平 ('flat, level') + 台 (臺, 'raised terrace, stage'): originally 'a flat-topped viewing terrace or roof terrace' in Classical architecture, and extended in modern Mandarin to a station 'platform' or a technical/digital/business 'platform'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 平台 (via 萌典)

平时.etymology: Temporal noun combining 平 ('ordinary, normal, peacetime') + 时 (時, 'time'): 'in normal times, ordinarily, usually'. Attested since Han–Tang historical prose.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 平时 (via 萌典)

平板.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 平 ('flat, level') + 板 ('board, plank, slab, panel'): 'flat board, wooden plank; flat panel' (and in contemporary Mandarin short for 平板电脑 'tablet computer').

history.meaning: flat board/plank; flat panel; tablet computer

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 平板 (via 萌典)

年.etymology: Ancient character (originally 秊 in oracle-bone and bronze scripts) showing a person (人) carrying a ripe stalk of grain (禾) on their back: originally 'harvest of grain' (which occurred once a year in northern China), hence 'year, annual, age, New Year'.

history.meaning: person carrying harvested grain = annual harvest -> year

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 年 (via 萌典)

年轻人.etymology: Three-character compound combining 年轻 ('young in years', literally 'years light in weight': 年 'years of age' + 轻 'light/few') + 人 ('person'): 'young person, youth, young people'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 年轻人 (via 萌典)

并.etymology: Merged simplified graph representing: (1) 並/竝 (two people 立 standing side by side: 'side by side, together, combine, and/moreover') and (2) 并 (two干 joined together: 'merge, annex, combine'). In Mandarin, 并 also serves as an emphatic adverb before negatives (并不 'not at all', 并非 'by no means').

morphemes.meaning: two figures side by side = together, combine, and

history.form: 並 (side by side, together) / 并 (combine, merge)

history.meaning: combine; side by side; and; (before negation) at all

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 并 (via 萌典)

广场.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 广 (廣, 'wide, broad, spacious') + 场 (場, 'open ground, square'): 'public square, plaza, piazza'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 广场 (via 萌典)

床.etymology: Phono-semantic/ideographic character (originally 牀, combining 爿 qiáng 'wooden frame/plank set on legs' + 木 'wood'; variant 床 places 木 under 广 'house shelter'): 'bed, couch' (and a bed-like frame or river bed).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 床 (via 萌典)

床单.etymology: Compound noun of 床 ('bed') + 单 (單, 'single cloth sheet'): 'bedsheet'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 床单 (via 萌典)

床头.etymology: Locative compound noun of 床 ('bed') + 头 (頭, 'head/end'): 'head of the bed, bedside'. Famously in Li Bai's 床前明月光 / 床头.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 床头 (via 萌典)

应急.etymology: Verb-object compound used as a verb and modifier, combining 应 (應, read yìng, 'respond to, deal with, meet') + 急 ('urgent need, emergency'): 'respond to an emergency, meet an urgent need; emergency (modifier, e.g., 应急灯 emergency light)'.

history.stage: Classical Chinese (Hou Hanshu) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 应急 (via 萌典)

应该.etymology: Compound modal verb combining two necessity/obligation roots: 应 (應, yīng, 'ought to, fitting') + 该 (該, 'ought to, due'): 'should, ought to, must (epistemic)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 应该 (via 萌典)

底下.etymology: Locative compound combining 底 ('bottom, base, underside', shelter 广 + 氐 'lowest root') + 下 ('below, under', neutral tone xia): 'underneath, below, at the bottom'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 底下 (via 萌典)

店.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 广 ('building/roof') + 占 (zhàn/diàn phonetic): originally 'a roadside stand or storehouse for displaying goods', then 'inn, tavern, shop, store'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 店 (via 萌典)

店主.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 店 ('shop, inn') + 主 ('owner, proprietor, host'): 'shopkeeper, store owner, innkeeper'. Attested since Tang–Song tales and histories.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 店主 (via 萌典)

店员.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 店 ('shop, store') + 员 (員, 'staff member, clerk'): 'shop assistant, store clerk, salesclerk'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 店员 (via 萌典)

店长.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 店 ('shop, store') + 长 (長, read zhǎng, 'head, chief, manager'): 'store manager, shop manager'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 店长 (via 萌典)

店门.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 店 ('shop, store') + 门 (門, 'door, entrance'): 'shop door, storefront entrance'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 店门 (via 萌典)

度.etymology: Phono-semantic/ideographic character combining 庶 (shù/dù phonetic, reduced at top) + 又 ('hand', measuring by the span of the hand/arm): read dù as a noun and classifier meaning 'measure, degree (of temperature, angle, latitude, or electricity kWh), limit, tolerance, occasion/time'; read duó as a verb meaning 'surmise, estimate (揣度)'.

history.meaning: measure by hand; standard; degree (dù); estimate (duó)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 度 (via 萌典)

座.etymology: Phono-semantic/ideographic character formed by adding the building/shelter radical 广 to 坐 (zuò, 'sit'): 'seat, throne, pedestal/stand/base' and the standard classifier for large stationary objects that 'sit' firmly in place (mountains, bridges, buildings, cities, statues: 一座山, 一座桥).

history.meaning: seat; stand; classifier for mountains, bridges, buildings

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 座 (via 萌典)

座板.etymology: Compound noun of 座 ('seat') + 板 ('wooden board, flat panel'): 'seat board (of a chair, bench, or toilet seat)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 座板 (via 萌典)

庭院.etymology: Coordinative noun compound pairing 庭 ('open courtyard in front of the main hall', shelter 广 + 廷) + 院 ('walled courtyard compound', mound/wall 阝 + 完): 'courtyard, yard, garden court'. Famously in Ouyang Xiu's 庭院深深深几许.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 庭院 (via 萌典)

建筑.etymology: Coordinative verb and noun compound of 建 ('establish, set up upright', 聿 + 廴) + 筑 (築, 'ram earth with a wooden杵 pestle to build walls', 竹 + 巩 + 木): 'build, construct; building, architecture'.

history.meaning: set up and ram earth to construct

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 建筑 (via 萌典)

建筑师.etymology: Three-character occupational noun combining 建筑 ('architecture, building') + 师 (師, 'master, professional specialist'): 'architect'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 建筑师 (via 萌典)

开.etymology: Ancient ideogram (traditional 開) showing two hands (廾) lifting away the horizontal bolt (一) that bars a pair of double doors (門): 'unbolt and open a door -> open, unfold, start/begin, turn on/switch on, drive/operate a vehicle, boil (of water), hold (a meeting), write out (a receipt/prescription)'.

morphemes.meaning: two hands removing the door bar

history.meaning: two hands unbolting double doors = open, begin
open; turn on; start; drive; boil

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 开 (via 萌典)

开关.etymology: Antonymic verb-pair compound turned noun: 开 ('open / switch on', originally two hands lifting a bar from门 gate leaves) + 关 ('shut / switch off', a crossbar latching门 shut). By pairing opposite actions, 开关 names an electrical switch or valve.

history.meaning: opening and closing a gate or pass

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 开关 (via 萌典)

开头.etymology: Verb-object/noun compound of 开 ('open, begin') + 头 (頭, 'head, beginning, first end'): 'begin, start; the beginning, opening (of a story, speech, or event)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 开头 (via 萌典)

开始.etymology: Coordinative verb and noun compound of 开 ('open, initiate') + 始 ('begin, start', woman 女 + 台): 'begin, start; beginning'.

history.stage: Classical & Buddhist Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 开始 (via 萌典)

开幕.etymology: Verb-object compound of 开 ('open, draw back') + 幕 ('stage curtain'): literally 'raise/open the stage curtain', and by extension 'open (of a performance, exhibition, festival, or conference)'.

history.meaning: raise the curtain -> open (of a show, exhibition, or event)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 开幕 (via 萌典)

开心.etymology: Verb-object compound used as an adjective and verb, combining 开 ('open up, unfold') + 心 ('heart, mind'). In Tang poetry (Du Fu's 开心胸) it meant 'open one's heart frankly or relieve sorrow'; in modern Mandarin (reinforced by Cantonese and southern Mandarin usage) it is the everyday word for 'happy, joyful, glad, have fun'.

history.meaning: open one's heart; feel relieved and gladdened

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 开心 (via 萌典)

开放.etymology: Coordinative verb and adjective compound of 开 ('open') + 放 ('release, let go, blossom'): '(of flowers) bloom, blossom; open to the public; lift restrictions; open-minded'.

history.stage: Tang–Song poetry (blossoming flowers) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: bloom; open to the public; open-minded

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 开放 (via 萌典)

开衫.etymology: Compound garment noun of 开 ('open down the front') + 衫 ('unlined upper garment, shirt/sweater',衣 + 彡): 'cardigan, front-buttoning or front-opening sweater'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 开衫 (via 萌典)

开过.etymology: Verb + complement/aspect compound of 开 ('open, drive, bloom') + 过 (過, 'pass by; experiential aspect marker -guo'): either 'drive past / pass by' or 'have opened / have driven before'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 开过 (via 萌典)

开锁.etymology: Verb-object compound of 开 ('open, unlock') + 锁 (鎖, 'metal lock', metal 钅 + 贝): 'unlock a lock, pick or open a lock'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 开锁 (via 萌典)

开门.etymology: Verb-object compound of 开 ('open') + 门 (門, 'door, gate'): literally 'open the door' and commercially 'open for business (for the day)'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: open the door; open for business

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 开门 (via 萌典)

弄.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on bronze inscriptions showing two hands (廾) holding and playing with a piece of jade (王/玉): originally 'play with, handle,fondle (and play music)', and in colloquial Mandarin a versatile general action verb (read nòng, or literary lòng) meaning 'do, make, handle, fix, get, mess with'.

history.meaning: two hands handling jade = play with, handle, perform
do; make; handle; fix; cause to become

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 弄 (via 萌典)

弄坏.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining the general causative verb 弄 ('handle, do, make') + 坏 (壞, 'broken, ruined'): 'break, ruin, damage, mess up'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 弄坏 (via 萌典)

弄裂.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining 弄 ('handle, cause to become') + 裂 ('split, crack', 列 + 衣 'tear cloth'): 'crack, cause to split or crack'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 弄裂 (via 萌典)

弟弟.etymology: Reduplicated kinship noun from 弟 (originally leather thongs wrapped in sequential order around a spear shaft, hence 'junior in sequence -> younger brother'). In Mandarin, 弟弟 (dìdi) is the standard everyday word for 'younger brother'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 弟弟 (via 萌典)

张.etymology: Measure word for flat, spread-out surfaces and paper items (一张桌子 'a table', 一张纸 'a sheet of paper', 一张床 'a bed'). Formed from 弓 ('bow') + 长 (cháng phonetic), 張 originally meant 'string and draw a bow open' in the Shijing, extending naturally to things spread flat.

history.meaning: classifier for flat sheets, tables, beds

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 張 (via 萌典)

弹.etymology: Phono-semantic character (彈) combining 弓 ('bow') + 单 (單, dān/tán phonetic): originally 'shoot pellets with a crossbow/slingshot'. Read tán as a verb meaning 'pluck or play a stringed/keyboard instrument (guitar, piano, zither), flick with the fingers, spring/bounce back'; read dàn as a noun meaning 'pellet, bullet, bomb (子弹, 炸弹)'.

history.meaning: shoot a pellet bow; flick/pluck strings (tán); pellet/ball (dàn)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 弹 (via 萌典)

弹琴.etymology: Verb-object compound of 弹 (tán, 'pluck or strike musical strings/keys with the fingers') + 琴 ('ancient Chinese seven-stringed zither guqin -> stringed or keyboard instruments generally, especially the piano 钢琴'): 'play the zither, piano, or a keyboard/stringed instrument'. Attested since the Shijing.

history.meaning: play the zither -> play the piano or musical instrument

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 弹琴 (via 萌典)

当.etymology: Merged simplified graph (mainly from 當, combining 尚 shàng/dāng phonetic + 田 'fields of matching value'; also 噹): read dāng 'match, face, serve as / work as (当老师), ought to, just at (a time or place)'; read dàng 'treat as, consider right/proper, pawn (at a pawnshop)'.

history.meaning: fields of equal value -> match, face, ought to, act as (dāng); proper, fit (dàng)
work/serve as, when/at, ought (dāng); regard as, appropriate (dàng)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 当 (via 萌典)

当上.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining 当 (dāng, 'serve as, hold the role/post of') + 上 (complement of attainment 'successfully reach/assume'): 'become, land the role or post of'.

history.meaning: succeed in becoming; take up the role of

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 当上 (via 萌典)

当心.etymology: Verb-object compound of 当 ('place right at, bear in') + 心 ('heart, mind'): originally 'keep at the center of one's mind/attention', and in Mandarin 'be careful, watch out!, take care'.

history.meaning: pay heed -> be careful, watch out

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 当心 (via 萌典)

当然.etymology: Compound adjective and modal adverb of 当 (dāng, 'ought to be, fitting') + 然 ('so, thus'): in Classical prose 'rightly so, as it ought to be', and in modern Mandarin the everyday word for 'of course, naturally, certainly'.

history.meaning: what is naturally right and fitting

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 当然 (via 萌典)

影子.etymology: Colloquial noun formed from 影 ('shadow, reflection, image', combining 景 jǐng 'sunlight above a high tower' + 彡 'feathery rays/contours of shade') + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): 'shadow, reflection, silhouette, trace'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 影子 (via 萌典)

往.etymology: Ancient character attested on Shang oracle bones combining 彳 ('step along a road') + 主/生 (wǎng phonetic, originally a foot 止 above 土 'earth'): in Classical Chinese the verb 'go toward (a destination)', and in modern Mandarin the directional preposition 'toward, in the direction of, bound for' (as well as 'past' in 往事, 以往).

history.meaning: walk toward a destination; go; past

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 往 (via 萌典)

往上.etymology: Prepositional directional phrase combining 往 ('toward') + 上 ('up, upward'): 'upward, further up'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 往上 (via 萌典)

往外.etymology: Prepositional directional phrase combining 往 ('toward') + 外 ('outside, outward'): 'outward, toward the outside'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 往外 (via 萌典)

很.etymology: Degree adverb ('very') that also serves as the natural, unstressed link before simple predicate adjectives (今天很冷 'It is cold today'). In Classical Chinese (Shuo Wen Jie Zi, Zhanguo Ce), 很 meant 'unyielding, intractable, severe'; in Ming–Qing colloquial Mandarin that intensity bleached into the everyday degree word 'very'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 很 (via 萌典)

很久.etymology: Degree-modified temporal phrase combining 很 ('very') + 久 ('for a long time'): 'for a very long time, a long time'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 很久 (via 萌典)

很快.etymology: Degree-modified adverbial/adjectival phrase combining 很 ('very') + 快 ('fast, quick, soon'): 'very fast, very quickly, before long / very soon'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 很快 (via 萌典)

律师.etymology: Compound of 律 ('statute, law, rule') + 师 (師, 'master, specialist'). Originally a Buddhist monastic title in Medieval China for a monk versed in the Vinaya monastic code (律藏); in the late 19th century it was adopted as the modern legal term for 'lawyer, attorney-at-law'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 律师 (via 萌典)

得.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on Shang oracle bones showing a hand (寸/又) picking up a cowrie shell (貝, money) on the road (彳): 'obtain, get, gain'. From this core sense evolved three readings in Mandarin: (1) dé ('get, obtain, finish calculating/cooking: 好了/得了'), (2) neutral-tone de (post-verbal structural particle introducing a degree or resultative complement: 跑得快), and (3) děi ('must, have to, need').

morphemes.part: 旦 + 寸 (from 貝 + 寸)

history.meaning: hand finding shell currency on the road = obtain, get

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 得 (via 萌典)

得很.etymology: Post-adjectival intensifying complement combining the structural particle 得 (de) + 很 ('very'): placed after an adjective or stative verb (好得很, 忙得很) to mean 'very much indeed, extremely'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 得很 (via 萌典)

得救.etymology: Verb-object/passive compound combining 得 ('obtain, receive') + 救 ('rescue, deliverance'): 'be rescued, be saved (from danger)'.

history.stage: Classical & Buddhist Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: receive rescue = be saved, be rescued

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 得救 (via 萌典)

微笑.etymology: Modifier-head verb and noun compound of 微 ('slight, subtle, gentle') + 笑 ('smile, laugh'): 'smile gently, smile'. Attested since Chuci and Tang poetry (e.g., Bai Juyi's 回眸一笑百媚生 / 微笑).

history.stage: Classical & Tang poetry to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 微笑 (via 萌典)

心.etymology: Foundational pictograph (象形字) attested on Shang oracle bones and Zhou bronzes depicting the anatomical chambers and vessels of the physical heart: in Chinese thought, the seat of both emotion and cognition—'heart, mind, thought, feeling, intention, center/core'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: pictograph of the physical heart = heart, mind, center

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 心 (via 萌典)

心意.etymology: Coordinative noun compound of 心 ('heart') + 意 ('thought, intention, feeling'): 'one's sincere feelings, kind thought, regard, or token of appreciation'. Attested since Han–Six Dynasties poetry.

history.stage: Han–Six Dynasties poetry to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: thoughts and feelings of the heart; token of regard

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 心意 (via 萌典)

志豪.etymology: Chinese masculine given name combining 志 ('ambition, aspiration, high resolve', 士 + 心) + 豪 ('heroic, bold, outstanding talent'): 'Zhihao'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 志豪 (via 萌典)

志鹏.etymology: Chinese masculine given name combining 志 ('aspiration, ambition') + 鹏 (鵬, the mythical giant Peng bird of Zhuangzi whose wings span thousands of miles, symbolizing soaring ambition, 鹏程万里): 'Zhipeng'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 志鹏 (via 萌典)

忘.etymology: Ancient ideogram/phono-semantic character combining 亡 (wáng, 'lose, vanish, perish') + 心 ('heart, mind'): literally 'lose from the mind' = 'forget, overlook, neglect'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese (Shijing, Laozi) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 忘 (via 萌典)

忙.etymology: Phono-semantic character combining 忄 (心, 'heart, mind') + 亡 (wáng/máng phonetic, 'rush/lose'): originally 'flurried or pressed in mind', and from Tang–Song poetry and vernacular onward the standard word for 'busy, occupied; hurry, hasten'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 忙 (via 萌典)

忙乱.etymology: Coordinative adjective and verb compound of 忙 ('busy, hurried') + 乱 (亂, 'disordered, in a flurry/confusion'): 'rushed and flustered, in a frantic rush'.

history.meaning: hurried and confused; in a frantic rush

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 忙乱 (via 萌典)

忙活.etymology: Colloquial compound verb of 忙 ('be busy with') + 活 ('work, chores, livelihood', neutral tone huo): 'bustle about, work busily on chores or tasks'.

history.meaning: be busy working on chores or tasks

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 忙活 (via 萌典)

快.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 忄 (心, 'heart, mood') + 夬 (guài/kuài phonetic, 'part/decisive'). In Classical Chinese, 快 meant 'pleased, gladdened in heart, gratifying' (preserved in 快乐 'happy' and 痛快); from the Six Dynasties and Tang period onward, 'brisk and satisfying' shifted to 'fast, quick (in speed); sharp (of a blade); soon, about to'.

history.meaning: fast; quick; sharp; soon (about to); happy (in compounds)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 快 (via 萌典)

快点.etymology: Imperative and adverbial phrase combining 快 ('fast, quick') + 点 (short for 一点 'a little bit / somewhat', often rhotacized as 快点儿 kuàidiǎnr): 'hurry up!, a bit faster!, make it quick!'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 快点 (via 萌典)

快送.etymology: Modifier-head verb/noun compound of 快 ('fast, express') + 送 ('deliver, send'): 'express delivery, deliver quickly'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 快送 (via 萌典)

念.etymology: Ideographic/phono-semantic character attested in bronze inscriptions combining 今 (jīn, 'present, now', also phonetic in Old Chinese *krəm -> niàn) + 心 ('heart, mind'): originally 'hold present in the mind -> think of, miss, remember fondly', and from Medieval Buddhist sutra-chanting onward also 'read aloud, recite, study/attend school'.

history.meaning: keep in mind; think of; miss
read aloud; study; think of/miss; thought

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 念 (via 萌典)

念叨.etymology: Colloquial compound verb of 念 ('think of and speak about repeatedly') + 叨 ('talk on and on', neutral tone dao): 'talk about someone/something fondly or repeatedly, harp on, muse aloud'.

history.meaning: talk about repeatedly; fondly mention; mutter

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 念叨 (via 萌典)

念念.etymology: Reduplication of 念 ('keep in mind, murmur/read aloud'): used in idioms like 念念不忘 ('bear constantly in mind without ever forgetting') and colloquially for 'read aloud a bit, murmur repeatedly'.

history.stage: Classical & Buddhist Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: thought after thought; bear constantly in mind; read aloud a bit

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 念念 (via 萌典)

怎么.etymology: Interrogative adverb asking 'how?' or 'how come?' directly before a verb (怎么走？ 'how do I get there?', 怎么拿错了？ 'how did it get mixed up?'). Formed with the same colloquial -么 suffix as 什么 and attested throughout Ming–Qing vernacular fiction.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 怎麼 (via 萌典)

怎么办.etymology: Interrogative verb phrase combining 怎么 ('how?') + 办 (辦, 'handle, manage, do'): 'what's to be done?, how should we handle this?, what do I do?'.

history.meaning: what to do?; how to handle it?

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 怎么办 (via 萌典)

怎么样.etymology: Interrogative and indefinite pronoun/adjective combining 怎么 ('how?') + 样 (樣, 'appearance, manner, condition'): 'how is it?, what is it like?, how about it?'.

history.meaning: how is it?; what is it like?; how about…?

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 怎么样 (via 萌典)

怕.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 忄 (心, 'heart') + 白 (bái/pà phonetic). In Classical Chinese, 怕 (read bó, interchangeable with 泊) meant 'tranquil, unmoved in heart' (淡泊); from the Tang dynasty onward, read pà, it became the everyday verb for 'fear, be afraid of' and modal 'I'm afraid that /恐怕'.

history.meaning: fear; be afraid of; perhaps / I'm afraid that

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 怕 (via 萌典)

思考.etymology: Coordinative verb and noun compound of 思 ('think, ponder, reflect', field/skull 囟 above heart 心) + 考 ('examine, probe, verify'): 'think deeply, ponder, reflect on'. Attested since the Classic of History (Shangshu) commentary and Han prose.

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: ponder and examine; reflect deeply; think

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 思考 (via 萌典)

急.etymology: Phono-semantic character combining 及 (jí, 'catch up with, reach urgently', showing a hand seizing a person from behind) + 心 ('heart'): 'urgent, pressing; anxious, worried, impatient; fast/rapid (of current or rain); emergency'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 急 (via 萌典)

急事.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 急 ('urgent, pressing') + 事 ('matter, affair, business'): 'urgent matter, pressing business, emergency'. Attested since Han–Tang historical prose.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 急事 (via 萌典)

急匆匆.etymology: ABB-pattern vivid descriptive adjective and adverb combining 急 ('urgent, hurried') + reduplicated 匆 (匆, 'hasty, hurried'): 'in a great hurry, rushing hurriedly'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 急匆匆 (via 萌典)

性格.etymology: Compound noun of 性 ('innate nature, disposition', heart 忄 + 生 'born with') + 格 ('pattern, framework, character'): 'personality, character, temperament'. Used in Classical poetry criticism for poetic temperament and standardized in modern Chinese for human personality.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 性格 (via 萌典)

怪.etymology: Ideographic/phono-semantic character combining 忄 (心, 'heart, mind') + 圣 (originally 𢀖 'till the soil with hands', phonetic guài): 'feel something strange in mind -> strange, odd, weird; monster; blame, find fault with; (colloquial degree adverb) quite, rather (怪好看的)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 怪 (via 萌典)

怪不得.etymology: Potential verb-complement phrase of 怪 ('blame, wonder at') + 不得 ('cannot'): means literally 'one cannot blame (someone)' and, as a sentence adverb of sudden realization, 'no wonder!, so that's why!'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 怪不得 (via 萌典)

总.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 總, combining silk 糸 'tie cords together into a bundle' + 悤 cōng phonetic): originally 'bind silk threads together -> gather, sum up, overall, chief/general (总经理)', and as an adverb 'always, invariably, sooner or later, after all'.

morphemes.part: 丷 + 口 + 心 (from 總)

history.meaning: bind threads together; gather; chief; overall

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 总 (via 萌典)

总是.etymology: Temporal and modal adverb combining 总 (總, 'invariably, always') + 是 (focus/copular formative): 'always, invariably'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 总是 (via 萌典)

您.etymology: Polite singular second-person pronoun ('you'), formed by placing 你 ('you') above 心 ('heart') to signal respectful deference. Emerging in Jin and Yuan dynasty northern vernacular (originally fused from plural 你们 in polite address), 您 became Standard Mandarin's courteous pronoun for elders, teachers, and guests.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 您 (via 萌典)

您好.etymology: Polite Mandarin greeting ('hello'), substituting respectful 您 ('you') for everyday 你 before 好 ('well'). Used when greeting guests at a front desk, teachers, or elders.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 您好 (via 萌典)

惊讶.etymology: Coordinative adjective and verb compound of 惊 (驚, 'startled, shying like a frightened horse', 敬 + 馬) + 讶 (訝, 'amazed, exclaim in surprise', speech 讠 + 牙): 'surprised, astonished, amazed'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 惊讶 (via 萌典)

想.etymology: Mental and modal verb meaning 'think of, miss, would like to', combining 相 ('observe, mutual appearance', phonetic xiāng) above 心 ('heart-mind'). Attested in Han-dynasty texts for calling an image to mind, 想 before another verb expresses a polite wish ('would like to') softer than direct 要.

history.meaning: call to mind; long for; think

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 想 (via 萌典)

想起来.etymology: Verb + complex directional complement combining 想 ('think, recall') + 起来 (inchoative/emergent complement 'come up into awareness'): 'remember, recall, call to mind (something previously forgotten)'.

history.meaning: recall; remember; bring back to mind

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 想起来 (via 萌典)

意外.etymology: Modifier-head compound of 意 ('expectation, thought', 音 + 心) + 外 ('outside, beyond'): literally 'beyond what one expected', functioning as an adjective ('unexpected, surprising') and a noun ('accident, mishap, surprise'). Attested since the Zuozhuan and Shiji.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 意外 (via 萌典)

意思.etymology: Coordinative noun compound of 意 ('meaning, thought, intention') + 思 ('thought, sentiment', neutral tone si in this word): one of Mandarin's richest everyday nouns, meaning 'meaning, sense (of a word); opinion/idea; hint/sign; token of appreciation; interest/fun (有意思)'.

history.meaning: meaning; idea; hint; token of regard; fun/interest

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 意思 (via 萌典)

愿意.etymology: Verb-object/coordinative compound of 愿 (願, 'wish, desire sincerely') + 意 ('wish, intention'): 'be willing to, wish, want, ready to'.

history.stage: Han–Six Dynasties Buddhist & vernacular Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 愿意 (via 萌典)

慌.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 忄 (心, 'heart, mind') + 荒 (huāng, 'barren, overgrown, confused'): 'flustered, panicked, nervous, in a flurry; (as a post-verbal complement with 得) unbearable (累得慌)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 慌 (via 萌典)

慢.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 忄 (心, 'heart, attitude') + 曼 (màn, 'drawn out, long'). In Classical Chinese, 慢 meant 'negligent, remiss, disrespectful, haughty' (怠慢, 傲慢); from the Six Dynasties and Tang period onward, 'unhurried/lax' became the primary Mandarin word for 'slow (opposite of 快 'fast'); wait/hold on'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 慢 (via 萌典)

慢慢.etymology: Reduplication of the adjective/adverb 慢 ('slow'): 'slowly, unhurriedly, take one's time, gradually'.

history.stage: Tang–Song poetry & vernacular to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 慢慢 (via 萌典)

慢用.etymology: Polite dining formula combining 慢 ('slowly, take your time') + 用 ('partake of food/drink', polite verb for 'eat/drink'): 'please enjoy your meal, take your time eating'.

history.stage: Ming–Qing polite vernacular to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: take your time enjoying your meal; bon appétit

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 慢用 (via 萌典)

懂.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 忄 (心, 'heart, mind') + 董 (dǒng, 'supervise, set straight'): originally 'confused in mind (懵懂)', then in Song–Ming vernacular inverted/stabilized as the primary everyday verb for 'understand, comprehend, know'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 懂 (via 萌典)

懂行.etymology: Verb-object compound used as an adjective and verb, combining 懂 ('understand, know inside out') + 行 (read háng, 'trade, profession, line of business'): 'know the ropes, be an expert/insider in the trade'.

history.meaning: know the trade; be knowledgeable in a field

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 懂行 (via 萌典)

成.etymology: Ancient character attested on Shang oracle bones and Zhou bronzes combining 戊/戈 ('halberd/axe') + 丁 (dīng/chéng phonetic, 'nail/completeness'): 'accomplish, complete, succeed; become, turn into; established/ready-made; one-tenth (10%); okay/all right!'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 成 (via 萌典)

成都.etymology: Historic capital of Sichuan province, named in the Warring States period (after the phrase in the records of King Tai of Zhou: 一年成聚，二年成邑，三年成都 'in one year it became a settlement, in two years a town, in three years a capital'): 成 ('become, form into') + 都 ('capital city').

history.meaning: Chengdu (capital of Shu / Sichuan, kept the same name for over 2,300 years)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 成都 (via 萌典)

我.etymology: First-person singular pronoun ('I, me'), attested since Late Shang oracle-bone inscriptions, where the graph depicted a notched polearm before being borrowed phonetically for the first-person pronoun. In Classical Chinese texts such as the Classic of Poetry (Shijing) and Analects, 我 already serves unchanged as both subject 'I' and object 'me'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 我 (via 萌典)

我们.etymology: First-person plural pronoun ('we, us'), combining 我 ('I') with the human plural suffix 们 (men). Plural markers written 弭, 伟, 懣, and finally 們 appear in Song and Yuan vernacular literature to form collective personal pronouns.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 我們 (via 萌典)

或者.etymology: Disjunctive conjunction and adverb originally formed in Classical Chinese (Mencius, Zuozhuan) from indefinite pronoun 或 ('someone, some') + nominalizer 者 ('one who') = 'someone, perhaps'. In Medieval and Modern Mandarin it evolved into the conjunction 'or (in declarative statements and possibilities)' and adverb 'perhaps, maybe'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 或者 (via 萌典)

戴.etymology: Phono-semantic character combining 異 ('raise both hands to place something on the head') + 戈 (𢦏 zāi/dài phonetic): in Classical Chinese 'carry on top of the head, respect/support (拥戴)', and in Mandarin the specific verb for 'wear or put on accessories on the head, face, neck, hands, or body (hat, glasses, watch, scarf, gloves, ring, badge)'.

morphemes.meaning: hands placing an item on the head

history.meaning: bear on the head; honor and support

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 戴 (via 萌典)

房.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 户 ('single-leaf door, household') + 方 (fāng, 'side, quarter'): originally 'a side room flanking the central hall (堂) of a traditional courtyard house', and from the Han–Tang period onward the general noun for 'house, building, room, chamber'.

history.meaning: side chamber flanking a main hall

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 房 (via 萌典)

房东.etymology: Compound noun of 房 ('house, property') + 东 (東, short for 东家/主人 'host, master, owner', because in traditional Chinese etiquette the host sat on the eastern side 东阶 while the guest sat on the west): 'landlord, landlady, homeowner'.

history.meaning: master/owner of the house = landlord, landlady

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 房东 (via 萌典)

房产.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 房 ('house, building') + 产 (產, 'property, estate, asset'): 'real estate, house property, residential or commercial buildings owned'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 房产 (via 萌典)

房号.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 房 ('room') + 号 (號, 'number'): 'room number (in a hotel, apartment, or office building)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 房号 (via 萌典)

房子.etymology: Colloquial noun formed from 房 ('house, building, room') + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): 'house, apartment, building, room'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 房子 (via 萌典)

房梁.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 房 ('house, roof') + 梁 ('horizontal wooden bridge or roof beam', 水 + 刃 + 木): 'roof beam, main crossbeam of a house'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 房梁 (via 萌典)

房租.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 房 ('house, room') + 租 ('rent, tax', grain 禾 + 且): 'rent for a house or room'.

history.stage: Song–Ming commercial vernacular to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 房租 (via 萌典)

房间.etymology: Everyday two-syllable noun for 'room' (counted with 间: 一间房间), pairing 房 ('side house, chamber', attested in the Shijing) with 间 ('architectural bay, room space').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 房間 (via 萌典)

所以.etymology: Originally a Classical Chinese relative phrase combining 所 (object nominalizer 'that which') + 以 ('by means of, because of') = 'that by which, the reason why' (e.g., 所以然). Because 'the reason why [result happens]' introduced the consequence clause after a cause, it grammaticalized into the conjunction 'therefore, so, as a result'.

history.meaning: that by which; the reason why

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 所以 (via 萌典)

所有.etymology: Originally a Classical Chinese relative phrase of 所 ('that which') + 有 ('possess, have') = 'what one possesses, one's possessions' (retained in 所有权 'ownership'). By extension ('everything that exists/is had'), it became the universal quantifier determiner 'all, every'.

history.meaning: that which one possesses; everything there is

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 所有 (via 萌典)

扁豆.etymology: Descriptive botanical compound of 扁 ('flat, compressed') + 豆 ('bean, legume', originally a pictograph of a footed food vessel in oracle-bone script, transferred to pulses served in it), naming flat-seeded lentils and hyacinth beans.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 扁豆

扇.etymology: Ideogram combining 户 ('door') + 羽 ('bird wings/feathers'): originally 'woven bamboo or wooden door leaf' (because paired door leaves swing open like wings), then 'hand fan' (made of feathers, silk, or bamboo) and the standard classifier for doors and windows (一扇门, 一扇窗); read shān as the verb 'fan, flap, slap'.

history.meaning: fan; classifier for doors/windows (shàn); fan with a hand/fan (shān)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 扇 (via 萌典)

手.etymology: Foundational pictograph (象形字) attested from Shang oracle bones depicting a human hand with five fingers and wrist: 'hand; hold in hand; person skilled in a craft or activity (-er, as in 歌手, 新手); personally; convenient'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: pictograph of a five-fingered hand = hand; skill; specialist

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 手 (via 萌典)

手写.etymology: Noun-verb compound used as a verb and modifier, combining 手 ('by hand') + 写 (寫, 'write'): 'write by hand; handwritten'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 手写 (via 萌典)

手指.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 手 ('hand') + 指 ('finger, digit, point'): 'finger' (disambiguating fingers of the hand from toes 脚趾).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 手指 (via 萌典)

手电筒.etymology: Three-character compound combining 手 ('hand-held') + 电 ('electric') + 筒 ('tubular bamboo cylinder'): 'flashlight, electric torch' (named for its cylindrical battery tube held in the hand).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 手电筒 (via 萌典)

手脚.etymology: Coordinative noun compound pairing 手 ('hands') + 脚 ('feet'): means literally 'hands and feet, limbs', and figuratively 'movements/motions (手脚快 nimble)', 'chore effort (费手脚)', or 'secret underhanded tricks (做手脚)'.

history.meaning: hands and feet; movements; secret tampering

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 手脚 (via 萌典)

手表.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 手 ('hand, wrist') + 表 (錶, 'timepiece, watch'): 'wristwatch'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 手表 (via 萌典)

才.etymology: Pictograph in Shang oracle-bone script of a sprouting plant shoot pushing through the soil with roots below: originally 'natural endowment, talent, timber/ability (人才, 才能)'. Also used (merging 纔 cái) as the restrictive temporal and focus adverb 'just now; only then (after a condition or late time); only'.

morphemes.meaning: plant shoot = talent, ability; (for 纔) just, only then

history.form: 才 (talent, ability) / 纔 (just, only then)
history.meaning: sprouting shoot = innate talent; adverb 'only then, just'
only then; just now; only; talent/ability

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 才 (via 萌典)

扒.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 八 (bā/pá phonetic, 'part/divide'): read bā 'strip off, peel, pull down, cling to, push aside/dig up'; read pá 'rake together,扒饭 (shovel rice into the mouth), braise/stew, pickpocket'.

history.meaning: pull apart, cling to, dig/push aside (bā); rake, scoop, braise (pá)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 扒 (via 萌典)

打.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 丁 (dīng/dǎ phonetic, originally a nail head).
