Originally 'strike, hit, beat', and from the Tang–Song vernacular onward bleached into Mandarin's most prolific light verb across dozens of everyday actions ('make a phone call, take a taxi, fetch water, open, sweep, give a discount, play ball, knit'); also read dá for 'a dozen (12)'.

history.meaning: hit; light verb for everyday actions (dǎ); dozen (dá)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 打 (via 萌典)

打九折.etymology: Commercial verb-object phrase combining 打 ('give/apply a discount') + 九折 ('nine-tenths of the original price'): 'give a 10% discount (charge 90% of the list price)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 打九折 (via 萌典)

打开.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining 打 ('strike, act upon') + 开 (開, 'open'): 'open up (a door, window, box, book, or file); turn on / switch on (a light, TV, computer, or faucet)'.

history.meaning: open up; unfold; turn on / switch on

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 打开 (via 萌典)

打扫.etymology: Compound verb of 打 (light verb marking deliberate action) + 扫 (掃, 'sweep with a broom'): 'sweep, clean up, tidy (a room or courtyard)'. Attested since Song–Yuan vernacular.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 打扫 (via 萌典)

打扰.etymology: Polite compound verb of 打 (light verb) + 扰 (擾, 'disturb, trouble, throw into disorder'): 'disturb, bother, trouble, interrupt someone' (often used politely as 'sorry to bother you / excuse me for intruding').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 打扰 (via 萌典)

打招呼.etymology: Separable verb-object phrase combining 打 (light verb) + 招呼 ('call out and beckon with the hand', 招 'beckon with hand' + 呼 'call with voice'): 'greet someone, say hello, give advance notice'.

history.meaning: greet; say hello; give a heads-up

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 打招呼 (via 萌典)

打电话.etymology: Separable verb-object phrase combining 打 (light verb, originally from cranking/ringing early magneto telephones) + 电话 ('telephone', 电 'electric' + 话 'speech'): 'make a phone call'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 打电话 (via 萌典)

打磨.etymology: Compound verb of 打 ('work on, strike') + 磨 ('grind, polish, rub smooth on a whetstone'): 'sand, polish, buff, grind smooth (wood, metal, jade, or figuratively a piece of writing)'.

history.stage: Song–Ming craft vocabulary to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: grind and polish smooth; sand; refine

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 打磨 (via 萌典)

打算.etymology: Compound verb and noun of 打 (light verb) + 算 ('calculate, reckon, plan'): 'plan, intend (to do); plan, intention'. Attested from Song–Ming vernacular.

history.meaning: reckon and plan; intend to; plan

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 打算 (via 萌典)

扔.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 乃 (nǎi/rēng phonetic): originally 'pull, draw near' in Classical dictionaries, and in northern Mandarin the everyday verb for 'throw, toss; throw away, discard'.

history.stage: Ming–Qing northern vernacular to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 扔 (via 萌典)

扫.etymology: Ideogram (traditional 掃) combining 扌 (手, 'hand') + 帚 ('broom', depicting a bundle of twigs tied to a handle): 'sweep with a broom, clear away; sweep across (with the eyes or a scanner)'. Read sǎo as a verb ('sweep') and sào in nouns like 扫帚 ('broom').

history.meaning: hand holding a broom = sweep, clear away

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 扫 (via 萌典)

扳手.etymology: Compound tool noun combining 扳 (bān, 'pull or turn a lever/handle by hand', 扌 + 反) + 手 ('hand / tool handle'): 'wrench, spanner'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 扳手 (via 萌典)

找.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 戈 (gē). A vernacular character that emerged in Medieval–Ming Chinese (linked to 爪 zhǎo 'claw/grope for' and 划 huá 'row') as the everyday verb for 'look for, search for, seek; call on someone; give change (找钱)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 找 (via 萌典)

找到.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining the search verb 找 ('look for') + the attainment complement 到 ('reach, succeed in finding'): 'find (succeed in locating what one was looking for)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 找到 (via 萌典)

找回.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining 找 ('look for') + 回 ('return, get back'): 'find and get back, recover, retrieve'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 找回 (via 萌典)

把.etymology: Measure word for objects you grip by a handle or back (一把钥匙 'a key', 一把椅子 'a chair') AND disposal coverb fronting a definite object before an action verb (把门打开). Both functions grew directly out of the Classical Chinese verb 把 ('grasp, hold in the hand', combining 扌 'hand' + 巴 phonetic).

history.meaning: hold or grasp in the hand
classifier for handled items; object-fronting marker

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 把 (via 萌典)

把手.etymology: Compound noun of 把 ('grasp, hold, handle', 扌 + 巴) + 手 ('hand', neutral tone shou when meaning 'handle/knob'): 'handle, grip, knob, pull (of a door, drawer, or tool)' (read bǎshou; contrast bǎshǒu 'person who guards a pass or skilled hand').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 把手 (via 萌典)

抓住.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining 抓 ('grab, clutch, seize with the hand/claws', 扌 + 爪) + 住 ('hold fast, firmly'): 'grab hold of, catch, grip tightly, seize (an opportunity or person)'.

history.meaning: grab and hold fast; catch; seize

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 抓住 (via 萌典)

折.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on Shang oracle bones and Zhou bronzes showing an axe (斤) cutting a tree branch in two (斷/艸, later written as 扌): 'snap, break, bend, fold, turn back, convert/discount (at tenths of full price)'. Read zhé ('fold, break, discount'), shé ('snap in two, lose money'), and zhē ('turn over, pour back and forth').

history.meaning: axe snapping a bough = break, bend, fold

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 折 (via 萌典)

折叠.etymology: Coordinative verb compound of 折 ('bend, fold over') + 叠 (疊, 'pile up in layers, fold'): 'fold up, fold over'. Attested since Tang–Song poetry and prose.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 折叠 (via 萌典)

折叠椅.etymology: Three-character compound combining 折叠 ('folding, collapsible') + 椅 ('chair'): 'folding chair'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 折叠椅 (via 萌典)

折扣.etymology: Merchant accounting compound of 折 ('break off, reduce proportionally') + 扣 ('hold back, deduct from a sum'). In Chinese shopkeeper usage, 打九折 states the fraction retained (9/10 = 90%), whereas 折扣 names the price reduction itself.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 折扣 (via 萌典)

折纸.etymology: Verb-object compound and noun of 折 ('fold') + 纸 (紙, 'paper'): 'fold paper; paper folding, origami'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 折纸 (via 萌典)

抢.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 搶, combining 扌 'hand' + 倉 cāng/qiǎng phonetic): 'snatch, grab by force, rob; vie/scramble to be first (抢着做); rush against time (抢修)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 抢 (via 萌典)

报纸.etymology: Compound of 报 ('report, gazette, bulletin', as in imperial 邸报 court gazettes) + 纸 ('paper', silk/fibre radical 纟 + 氏, perfected during the Eastern Han).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 报纸 (via 萌典)

抬.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 台 (tái phonetic; also written 擡 with 臺): 'lift up, raise (one's head, hand, or eyes); carry a heavy object together between two or more people'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 抬 (via 萌典)

抬头.etymology: Verb-object compound of 抬 ('lift, raise') + 头 (頭, 'head'): 'raise one's head, look up' (and on invoices or receipts, the 'payee/header line').

history.meaning: raise one's head; look up; invoice header

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 抬头 (via 萌典)

抱.etymology: Phono-semantic/ideographic character of 扌 (手, 'hand/arms') + 包 (bāo, 'wrap, enfold'): 'hold in one's arms, embrace, hug; cherish/harbor (hope or an attitude); classifier for armfuls'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese (Shijing, Laozi) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: enfold in the arms; hug; hold; cherish

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 抱 (via 萌典)

抽.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 由 (yóu/chōu phonetic): 'pull out, draw out (a thread, lot, or drawer), pump/extract, whip/lash, shrink, smoke (inhale a cigarette)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 抽 (via 萌典)

抽屉.etymology: Compound furniture noun of 抽 ('pull out, draw forth') + 屉 (屜, originally a removable bamboo/wooden tray, pad, or tier inside a container, neutral tone ti): 'pull-out compartment -> drawer (of a desk or cabinet)'.

history.meaning: sliding drawer of a table or cabinet

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 抽屉 (via 萌典)

担心.etymology: Separable verb-object compound of 担 (擔, dān, 'carry on the shoulders, bear a load') + 心 ('heart, mind'): literally 'carry a burden on one's heart' -> 'worry, feel anxious, be concerned about'.

history.meaning: bear anxiety in one's heart = worry, be concerned

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 担心 (via 萌典)

拆.etymology: Phono-semantic/ideographic character combining 扌 (手, 'hand') + 斥 (chì, originally a cracked house/clod): 'split open, tear open (a letter or package), take apart, dismantle, demolish (a wall or old building)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 拆 (via 萌典)

拉.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 立 (lì/lā phonetic). In Classical Chinese (Mengzi, Shiji), 拉 meant 'snap, break, crush by pulling'; from the Tang–Song vernacular onward it became the primary verb for 'pull, drag, draw, haul; play a bowed string instrument (violin, erhu); chat; help along'.

history.meaning: pull; draw; drag; play a bowed instrument

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 拉 (via 萌典)

拉链.etymology: Compound noun combining 拉 ('pull') + 链 (鏈, 'interlocking metal chain'): 'zipper, slide fastener' (a descriptive calque of a chain fastened by pulling a slider).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 拉链 (via 萌典)

拍.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 白 (bái/pāi phonetic): 'pat, clap, slap with the flat of the hand; swat; musical beat/meter; racket/bat; take (a photograph or film, from clicking the shutter); auction (from banging the gavel)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 拍 (via 萌典)

拐.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 另 (lìng/guǎi, originally depicting a horned/forked walking staff): 'turn a corner, change direction; limp/hobble; walking stick (拐杖); abduct/swindle'.

history.meaning: turn a corner; crutch/walking stick; limp; swindle

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 拐 (via 萌典)

拐弯.etymology: Separable verb-object compound of 拐 ('turn') + 弯 (彎, 'curve, bend, corner'): 'turn a corner, make a turn, go around a bend'.

history.meaning: turn a corner; go around a bend

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 拐弯 (via 萌典)

拒绝.etymology: Coordinative verb compound of 拒 ('ward off, resist, fend off with the hand', 扌 + 巨) + 绝 (絕, 'sever a silk thread -> cut off completely'): 'refuse, reject, decline, turn down'. Attested since the的后汉书 Book of the Later Han.

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese (Hou Hanshu) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: fend off and cut off -> refuse, reject, decline

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 拒绝 (via 萌典)

招手.etymology: Verb-object compound of 招 ('beckon with the hand') + 手 ('hand'): 'wave one's hand, beckon with the hand'. Attested since Classical prose and Tang poetry.

history.stage: Classical & Tang Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 招手 (via 萌典)

招牌.etymology: Compound noun of 招 ('beckon, attract customers') + 牌 ('wooden or painted signboard, plaque'): originally the hanging wooden or cloth shop sign outside Song–Ming taverns and stores, and figuratively 'trademark, signature specialty, reputation'.

history.stage: Song–Ming urban commerce to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: shop signboard; signature specialty or reputation

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 招牌 (via 萌典)

拧.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 擰, combining 扌 'hand' + 寧 níng phonetic): read拧 nǐng ('twist, turn a knob/cap/screw, wring out a wet towel'), níng ('pinch and twist skin'), and nìng ('stubborn, cross-grained').

history.meaning: twist, turn, wring out (nǐng); pinch (níng); stubborn (nìng)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 拧 (via 萌典)

拱窗.etymology: Architectural compound noun combining 拱 ('arch, cup the hands together in an arch', 扌 + 共) + 窗 ('window'): 'arched window'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 拱窗 (via 萌典)

拱门.etymology: Compound of 拱 ('join hands in a curved bow; arch', hand classifier 扌 + phonetic 共 gǒng) + 门 ('gate, doorway', pictograph of double swinging gate leaves), naming a curved stone or brick archway.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 拱门 (via 萌典)

拿.etymology: Ideogram (会意字, variant of 拏) combining 合 ('join together, close') + 手 ('hand'): literally 'close the hand upon something' = 'take, hold, carry in the hand, fetch, seize', and in spoken Mandarin also an instrumental preposition ('with, using').

history.stage: Han–Tang Chinese (拏 / 拿) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: grasp with the hand; take; hold; fetch

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 拿 (via 萌典)

拿走.etymology: Resultative/directional verb compound combining 拿 ('take in the hand') + 走 ('walk away, leave'): 'take away, carry off'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 拿走 (via 萌典)

挂.etymology: Phono-semantic character (掛) combining 扌 (手, 'hand') + 圭 (guī/guà phonetic): originally 'suspend or divide counting stalks in Yijing divination', hence 'hang, hang up (a coat, picture, or phone), hook, register (a letter or hospital appointment), worry about (挂念)'.

history.meaning: set aside/suspend divination stalks -> hang up, suspend

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 挂 (via 萌典)

挂不住.etymology: Potential verb-complement compound combining 挂 ('hang') + 不 ('not') + 住 ('hold fast'): means literally 'cannot hang/stay on firmly (keeps slipping off)', and figuratively in 脸上挂不住 'unable to save face, feel embarrassed'.

history.meaning: cannot stay hung on; feel embarrassed / lose face

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 挂不住 (via 萌典)

挂号信.etymology: Three-character postal compound combining 挂号 ('register a serial number in an official ledger', 挂 'enter/list' + 号 'number') + 信 ('letter'): 'registered letter, registered mail'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 挂号信 (via 萌典)

挂断.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining 挂 ('hang up a telephone receiver') + 断 (斷, 'cut off, disconnect'): 'hang up the phone, disconnect a call'.

history.meaning: hang up the telephone; end a call

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 挂断 (via 萌典)

挂钟.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 挂 ('hang on a wall') + 钟 (鐘, 'clock'): 'wall clock'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 挂钟 (via 萌典)

指.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 旨 (zhǐ phonetic): 'finger, digit' and verbally 'point at, point out, indicate, direct, count on (指望)'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese (Shijing, Mencius) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: finger; point at; indicate; refer to

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 指 (via 萌典)

指南.etymology: Verb-object compound of 指 ('point toward') + 南 ('south'). Originated in ancient Chinese magnetic south-pointing instruments (指南车 'south-pointing chariot' and 指南针 'magnetic compass', which in Chinese tradition is described as pointing south rather than north), and broadened metaphorically to mean 'guide, guidebook, handbook'.

history.meaning: point south (of a compass or chariot)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 指南 (via 萌典)

按.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 安 (ān/àn, 'settle down'): 'press down with the hand or finger (a button, key, or doorbell); hold back/restrain; check; according to (preposition, short for 按照)'.

history.meaning: press down with the hand; halt; examine

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 按 (via 萌典)

挞底.etymology: Culinary compound combining 挞 (撻, tà, phonetic loan for Western pastry 'tart') + 底 ('bottom, base'): 'tart shell, pastry crust base'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 挞底 (via 萌典)

挡.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 擋, combining 扌 'hand' + 當 dāng/dǎng phonetic): 'block, bar, keep out (wind, rain, or light), get in the way of; gear of a vehicle (read dǎng or dàng)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 挡 (via 萌典)

挥挥手.etymology: Reduplicated verb-object phrase from 挥手 (挥 'wave, brandish with the hand', 扌 + 军 + 手 'hand'): 'give a wave of the hand, wave goodbye or hello'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 挥挥手 (via 萌典)

挺.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 廷 (tíng, 'stand upright at court'): originally 'pull out, stand straight and upright, stick out (one's chest), hold out/endure', and in colloquial Mandarin a common degree adverb meaning 'quite, rather, pretty (挺好的)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 挺 (via 萌典)

换.etymology: Phono-semantic character (換) of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 奂 (奐, huàn phonetic, originally two hands passing something through an opening): 'exchange, swap, trade, change (clothes, money, trains, or parts), replace'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: exchange with the hands; replace; change

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 换 (via 萌典)

掉.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 卓 (zhuō/diào phonetic). In Classical Chinese, 掉 meant 'shake, wag, swing (as in 尾大不掉)' or 'turn around (掉头)'. From the Tang–Song vernacular onward it became the primary verb for 'fall, drop, lose, come off, fade' and a resultative complement of removal/disappearance (吃掉, 忘掉).

history.meaning: fall; drop; lose; resultative complement of removal

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 掉 (via 萌典)

排.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 非 (fēi/pái phonetic, whose symmetrical wings also suggest two aligned rows): originally 'push open, push aside (排山倒海)', then 'arrange in order, line up, rehearse, drain/discharge' and the noun/classifier for 'a row, line, or platoon'.

history.meaning: push open; push aside; arrange in order
arrange in a line; row (noun/classifier); rehearse; drain

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 排 (via 萌典)

接.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 妾 (qiè/jiē phonetic): 'come into contact, join together, connect; receive/catch in the hand; answer (the phone); meet/pick up someone (at a station or school); take over/continue'.

history.meaning: connect; receive; answer (the phone); pick up (a person)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 接 (via 萌典)

接口.etymology: Compound noun of 接 ('join, connect') + 口 ('opening, port, mouth'): literally 'joining opening/seam' (of pipes, carpentry joints, or clothing), and in modern technology 'interface, port, jack, connector'.

history.stage: Traditional craft to Modern technical Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 接口 (via 萌典)

接待.etymology: Coordinative verb compound of 接 ('receive, welcome a guest') + 待 ('treat, entertain, wait upon'): 'receive and attend to (guests, visitors, or clients); reception'. Attested since the Book of Rites (Liji) and Han histories.

history.stage: Classical Chinese (Liji, Hanshu) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 接待 (via 萌典)

推.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 隹 (zhuī/tuī phonetic): 'push forward with the hand (opposite of 拉 'pull'); shove; turn a millstone; infer/deduce (推理); recommend; postpone (推迟) or shirk'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese (Shijing, Mencius) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: push with the hand; advance; infer; recommend; put off

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 推 (via 萌典)

提.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 是 (shì/tí phonetic): 'carry hanging from the hand (a bag, bucket, or kettle); lift up, raise, promote; bring up/mention (a topic); move earlier in time (提前)'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: carry by hand; lift; raise; mention

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 提 (via 萌典)

插.etymology: Ideogram (会意字) showing a hand (扌) driving a pestle or pointed tool (千/干) into a mortar (臼): 'insert, stick in, plug in, plant (rice seedlings), interpose (a remark or episode)'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: pierce/insert into a socket = stick in, plug in, insert

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 插 (via 萌典)

插销.etymology: Compound hardware noun combining 插 ('insert, slide in') + 销 (銷, 'metal pin, peg, bolt'): 'sliding door/window bolt, latch pin' (and in some dialects an electrical plug).

history.meaning: sliding bolt or latch on a door or window

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 插销 (via 萌典)

搬.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 般 (bān, 'shift, transport by boat'): 'move, carry, shift (heavy objects or furniture from one place to another)'. Attested from Tang–Song vernacular onward.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 搬 (via 萌典)

搬家.etymology: Separable verb-object compound of 搬 ('move, shift') + 家 ('home, household'): 'move house, relocate one's home'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 搬家 (via 萌典)

搬家公司.etymology: Four-character compound combining 搬家 ('move house') + 公司 ('company'): 'moving company, household movers'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 搬家公司 (via 萌典)

搭档.etymology: Compound verb and noun of 搭 ('join together, pair up', 扌 + 荅) + 档 (檔, 'group, team, stage/business slot'): originally from traditional Chinese opera and storytelling for two performers teaming up on stage, now the general word for 'team up, cooperate; partner, teammate'.

history.stage: Qing–Republican performing arts to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 搭档 (via 萌典)

摆.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 擺, combining 扌 'hand' + 罷 bà/bǎi phonetic): 'set out, arrange, display, place (furniture, dishes, or goods); wave/swing back and forth (like a pendulum 钟摆); put on airs'.

history.meaning: arrange; set out; display; swing back and forth

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 摆 (via 萌典)

摊.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 攤, combining 扌 'hand' + 難 nán/tān phonetic): 'spread out flat on a surface; vendor's stall or booth (摆摊); fry a thin batter (pancake/omelet); share/divide costs equally; befall'.

history.meaning: spread out; vendor's stall; share a portion

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 摊 (via 萌典)

摘.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 啇 (dì/zhāi phonetic): 'pluck, pick (flowers, fruit, or tea leaves with the fingers); take off (glasses, a hat, or a hanging item); select/excerpt passages'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: pick/pluck with the hand; take off (glasses/hat); excerpt

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 摘 (via 萌典)

摸.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 莫 (mò/mō phonetic, which also means 'dusk/dark'): 'feel, touch, stroke gently with the hand; grope in the dark for; figure out/sound out (摸清)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 摸 (via 萌典)

摸摸.etymology: Reduplicated verb from 摸 ('touch, feel, stroke'): 'touch gently, give a pat or stroke, feel with one's hand'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 摸摸 (via 萌典)

撒.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 散 (sàn/sǎ phonetic, 'scatter'): read sǎ 'scatter, sprinkle, strew (seeds, salt, powder, or water), spill'; read sā 'let go, release, cast (a net), let oneself go (撒娇)'.

history.meaning: let go, cast (sā); scatter, sprinkle, spill (sǎ)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 撒 (via 萌典)

撞.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand/strike') + 童 (tóng/zhuàng phonetic): originally 'strike a bell or drum with a wooden ram', hence 'bump into, knock against, collide with, run into by chance'.

history.stage: Classical Chinese (Zhuangzi, Shiji) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: strike against; bump into; collide; meet by chance

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 撞 (via 萌典)

播放.etymology: Coordinative verb compound of 播 ('sow, spread abroad, broadcast', 扌 + 番) + 放 ('release, play back'): 'broadcast (over radio/TV) or play (recorded audio or video)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 播放 (via 萌典)

擦.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 扌 (手, 'hand') + 察 (chá/cā phonetic): 'rub, wipe clean (with a cloth or towel), scrub, erase, brush past closely, apply (ointment/lotion)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 擦 (via 萌典)

收.etymology: Ancient character attested on Shang oracle bones combining 丩 ('bind/gather together') + 攵 ('hand holding a stick/implement'): originally 'arrest/gather in, harvest crops', and by extension 'receive, accept (a gift, letter, or payment); put away/collect; bring to a close; restrain'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: gather in; harvest; receive; collect; put away

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 收 (via 萌典)

收据.etymology: Compound noun of 收 ('receive payment or goods') + 据 (據, 'written proof, voucher, certificate'): 'written receipt'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 收据 (via 萌典)

改.etymology: Ancient ideogram combining 己 ('self / coiled thread') + 攵 ('hand holding a rod'): 'correct faults -> change, alter, modify, revise, correct (homework/papers), switch to'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 改 (via 萌典)

改建.etymology: Compound verb of 改 ('change, alter, remodel') + 建 ('build, construct'): 'rebuild, remodel, reconstruct, convert (an existing building or structure)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 改建 (via 萌典)

放.etymology: Phono-semantic/ideographic character combining 方 (fāng phonetic, 'direction/outward') + 攵 ('hand with a stick driving or releasing'): originally 'drive out, banish, let go free', and from the Six Dynasties and Tang period onward also the primary Mandarin verb for 'put, place, set down; let out/turn on; blossom; have a holiday (放假)'.

history.meaning: let go; release; drive away; unrestrained
put/place; release; let off; bloom; play

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 放 (via 萌典)

放心.etymology: Separable verb-object compound of 放 ('set down, put at ease') + 心 ('heart, mind'): originally in Mencius (求其放心 'seek back one's lost/straying heart'), reinterpreted in Song–Ming vernacular as 'set one's heart at rest -> rest assured, stop worrying, feel at ease'.

history.meaning: put one's mind at rest; rest assured; not worry

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 放心 (via 萌典)

放进去.etymology: Verb + complex directional complement combining 放 ('put, place') + 进去 ('go inside, away from the speaker'): 'put inside, place in'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 放进去 (via 萌典)

故事.etymology: Modifier-head noun compound of 故 ('old, former, past') + 事 ('affair, event, practice'). In Classical Chinese (Hanshu, Tang histories), 故事 meant 'past events, historical precedents, established routine'. In Tang–Song popular storytelling (说话) it came to mean 'narrative tale, story, plot' (read gùshi with neutral tone).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 故事 (via 萌典)

救.etymology: Phono-semantic character combining 求 (qiú/jiù phonetic) + 攵 ('hand action'): originally 'stop/prevent evil', then 'succor, rescue, save (from danger, fire, or distress), relieve, help'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese (Shijing, Analects) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 救 (via 萌典)

救下.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining 救 ('rescue, save') + 下 (complement indicating successfully taking/keeping someone out of danger): 'rescue, save (from harm or danger)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 救下 (via 萌典)

救星.etymology: Metaphorical compound noun of 救 ('rescue, save') + 星 ('auspicious star'): literally 'saving star' -> 'savior, deliverer, lifesaver (person or thing that comes to the rescue in a pinch)'. Attested from Song–Yuan drama and vernacular.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 救星 (via 萌典)

教.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on Shang oracle bones showing a hand holding a teaching rod (攵) beside a child (子) learning counting/imitation marks (爻, i.e., 孝): read jiāo in spoken Mandarin for 'teach, instruct (someone a skill or subject)', and read jiào in compounds and nouns for 'instruct, education, religion (教育, 教室, 宗教)'.

history.meaning: hand with rod guiding a child = teach, instruct, education

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 教 (via 萌典)

敞开.etymology: Resultative verb compound of 敞 ('spacious, open wide, uncovered', 尚 + 攵) + 开 (開, 'open'): 'open wide (doors, windows, coats, or one's heart); unrestricted'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 敞开 (via 萌典)

敢.etymology: Ancient character attested on bronze inscriptions showing hands seizing a wild boar or obstacle with 攵: 'dare, have the courage or boldness to, venture to; (in questions/rhetorical phrases) how could one dare…'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: boldly confront = dare, venture to, courageous

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 敢 (via 萌典)

敬.etymology: Ancient ideogram combining 苟 (jí, showing a figure with horned/alert head Gear and mouth 口 speaking circumspectly, NOT the grass-radical 苟 gǒu) + 攵 ('hand action'): originally 'be reverently alert and circumspect', hence 'respect, revere, honor; offer politely (a toast, tea, or salute)'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: reverent alertness = respect, honor, offer respectfully

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 敬 (via 萌典)

敬重.etymology: Coordinative verb compound of 敬 ('respect, revere') + 重 ('value highly, attach great weight to'): 'respect deeply, hold in high esteem, revere'. Attested since the漢書 Book of Han.

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 敬重 (via 萌典)

数字.etymology: Compound noun of 数 (數, shù, 'number, count') + 字 ('written character, symbol'): 'numeral, digit, figure, number; digital'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 数字 (via 萌典)

敲.etymology: Phono-semantic character combining 高 (gāo/qiāo phonetic) + 攴/攵 ('hand holding a striker'): 'knock on, tap, strike, rap (a door, drum, table, or keyboard)'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese (Zuozhuan) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 敲 (via 萌典)

敲中.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining 敲 ('knock, strike, tap') + 中 (read zhòng in the fourth tone, 'hit the target/mark'): 'strike right on target, hit the mark by tapping/knocking'.

history.meaning: strike and hit the exact spot/target

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 敲中 (via 萌典)

敲击.etymology: Coordinative verb compound of 敲 ('knock, tap') + 击 (擊, 'strike, beat, hit'): 'rap, tap, percuss, strike repeatedly'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 敲击 (via 萌典)

敲门.etymology: Separable verb-object compound of 敲 ('knock on, rap') + 门 (門, 'door'): 'knock on the door' (famous from Jia Dao's Tang couplet 鸟宿池边树，僧敲月下门, the origin of 推敲 'weigh words carefully').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 敲门 (via 萌典)

整.etymology: Ideogram/phono-semantic character combining 敕 (bundle of wood 束 beaten into order by a hand 攵) + 正 (zhèng, 'straight, upright, exact'): 'put in order, tidy up, repair; whole, entire, full/exact (of round numbers or hours on the clock); (colloquially) fix/do/tease'.

history.meaning: put ranks/items in neat order; whole
whole; entire; exact; tidy up; mend

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 整 (via 萌典)

整个.etymology: Modifier-classifier compound determiner and adjective of 整 ('whole, entire') + 个 (個, general unit classifier): 'the whole, the entire'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 整个 (via 萌典)

整夜.etymology: Temporal compound of 整 ('whole, entire') + 夜 ('night'): 'the whole night, all night long'.

history.meaning: all night long; the entire night

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 整夜 (via 萌典)

整天.etymology: Temporal compound of 整 ('whole, entire') + 天 ('day'): 'all day long, the whole day'.

history.meaning: the whole day; all day long

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 整天 (via 萌典)

整排.etymology: Quantifier phrase combining 整 ('whole, entire') + 排 ('row, line'): 'the whole row, an entire row of'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 整排 (via 萌典)

整整.etymology: Reduplication of 整 ('whole, full'): used as an emphatic adverb before numeral-classifier phrases (整整三天 'a full three days') to mean 'a full, a whole, no less than'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 整整 (via 萌典)

整整齐齐.etymology: AABB-pattern vivid reduplication of the disyllabic adjective 整齐 ('neat, tidy, even'): 'neat and tidy, in apple-pie order, nicely aligned'.

history.form: 整整齊齊 / 整整齐齐
history.meaning: very neat and tidy; in perfect order

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 整整齐齐 (via 萌典)

整理.etymology: Coordinative verb compound of 整 ('put in neat order') + 理 ('cut and polish jade along its natural veins -> put in order, arrange, manage'): 'put in order, tidy up, sort out, organize, collate'. Attested since Han texts.

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: put in order; tidy up; sort out; organize

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 整理 (via 萌典)

整齐.etymology: Coordinative adjective and verb compound of 整 ('orderly, arranged') + 齐 (齊, 'even, uniform in height like ears of grain'): 'neat, tidy, even, well-ordered'. Attested since the Zuozhuan and Shiji.

history.stage: Classical Chinese (Zuozhuan, Shiji) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 整齐 (via 萌典)

文件.etymology: Compound noun of 文 ('writing, text') + 件 ('individual item, document'): 'official document, paper, file (physical or computer file)'.

history.stage: Qing administrative Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 文件 (via 萌典)

斜.etymology: Phono-semantic character combining 余 (yú/xié phonetic) + 斗 ('ladle/scoop'): originally 'ladle out liquid' (by tilting a scoop), hence 'tilted, slanting, oblique, diagonal, leaning (opposite of 正 'straight/upright')'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: tilted like a scooping ladle = slanting, oblique, diagonal

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 斜 (via 萌典)

断.etymology: Ancient ideogram (traditional 斷) showing an axe (斤) cutting through skeins of silk thread (㡭): 'cut in two, sever, snap, break off; stop/abstain from; judge/decide (判断); (in negative sentences) absolutely'.

history.meaning: axe severing silk threads = cut off, break, decide
break; snap; cut off; interrupt; judge

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 断 (via 萌典)

新.etymology: Ancient phono-semantic/ideographic character attested on Shang oracle bones combining 亲/辛 ('chisel/hazel tree') + 木 ('wood') + 斤 ('axe'): originally 'chop fresh firewood from a tree', hence 'new, fresh, newly, renew (opposite of 旧/老)'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: axe cutting fresh wood = new, fresh, newly

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 新 (via 萌典)

新手.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 新 ('new') + 手 ('hand -> person practicing a craft or skill'): 'new hand, novice, beginner, newcomer'. Attested since Tang–Song poetry and prose.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 新手 (via 萌典)

新鲜.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 新 ('new, fresh') + 鲜 (鮮, 'freshly caught fish/mutton -> fresh, bright, delicious', neutral tone xian in everyday speech): 'fresh (of food, flowers, or air); novel, new and unfamiliar'. Attested since Han–Six Dynasties prose.

history.meaning: fresh (not spoiled or stale); novel; new

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 新鲜 (via 萌典)

方格.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 方 ('square') + 格 ('grid, lattice, check'): 'square grid, check/plaid pattern, squared box on paper or fabric'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 方格 (via 萌典)

旁.etymology: Phono-semantic character combining 帝/凡 (broad/spread above) + 方 (fāng/páng phonetic): originally 'wide, spreading in all directions', then 'side, beside, nearby; other (旁人)'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 旁 (via 萌典)

旁边.etymology: Locative compound noun combining 旁 ('side, beside') + 边 (邊, 'edge, side'): 'beside, next to, by the side of'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 旁边 (via 萌典)

旅游.etymology: Coordinative verb and noun compound of 旅 ('travel away from home; troop of 500 soldiers marching under a banner 㫃') + 游 (遊, 'wander, roam, sightsee'): 'travel for pleasure, tour, sightseeing, tourism'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 旅游 (via 萌典)

旅行.etymology: Coordinative verb and noun compound of 旅 ('travel away from home') + 行 ('walk, go on a journey'): 'travel, take a trip, journey'.

history.meaning: travel in a group or on a journey

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 旅行 (via 萌典)

旋律.etymology: Sino-Japanese / literary Chinese musical compound combining 旋 ('revolve, return in phrases') + 律 ('pitch-pipe standard, musical law/temperament'). Standardized across modern East Asian musical terminology to render 'melody'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 旋律 (via 萌典)

无敌.etymology: Verb-object compound used as an adjective, combining 无 (無, 'have no, without') + 敌 (敵, 'match, rival, enemy'): 'have no match/equal -> invincible, unmatched, peerless' (from Mencius's 仁者无敌 'the benevolent person has no match in the world').

history.meaning: without match or rival; invincible; peerless

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 无敌 (via 萌典)

无盐.etymology: Verb-object/modifier phrase combining 无 (無, 'without, no') + 盐 (鹽, 'salt'): 'unsalted, salt-free (e.g., 无盐黄油 unsalted butter)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 无盐 (via 萌典)

无聊.etymology: Verb-object compound used as an adjective, combining 无 (無, 'have nothing') + 聊 ('rely on, find sustenance or solace in'). In Chuci and Shiji (民不聊生 / 无聊), 无聊 meant 'having nothing to rely on, destitute and despondent'; in modern Mandarin it means 'bored, boring, dull, silly/senseless'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 无聊 (via 萌典)

日子.etymology: Colloquial noun formed from 日 ('sun -> day') + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): means 'a specific day or date; days (count of time); everyday life or livelihood (过日子)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 日子 (via 萌典)

日期.etymology: Compound noun of 日 ('day') + 期 ('appointed time, date'): 'calendar date, appointed date'. Attested since the Zuozhuan and Shiji.

history.stage: Classical Chinese (Zuozhuan, Shiji) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 日期 (via 萌典)

旧.etymology: Simplified form of 舊 (originally an owl-like horned bird 萑 above a mortar 臼, borrowed phonetically in Old Chinese *gʷids -> jiù for 'old, former, past, used/worn, old friend'). Contrasts with 老 ('aged in years') by meaning 'used, old (opposite of 新 new), former'.

history.meaning: old (not new); former; long-standing; old friend

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 旧 (via 萌典)

旧事.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 旧 (舊, 'old, past, former') + 事 ('affair, event, matter'): 'past events, old matters, things of the past'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 旧事 (via 萌典)

旧物.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 旧 (舊, 'old, used, bygone') + 物 ('object, thing, article'): 'old object, keepsake from the past, secondhand/used item'.

history.stage: Classical & Tang–Song Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: old article; object from the past

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 旧物 (via 萌典)

早.etymology: Ideogram combining 日 ('sun') above 十/甲 ('first, armor/helm, or treetop'): 'the sun rising at the start of the day -> morning, early; long ago; (as a greeting) Good morning!'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: sun at first light = early, morning, 'Good morning!'

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 早 (via 萌典)

早上.etymology: Everyday noun for 'morning' (early morning until around nine or ten o'clock), combining 早 ('early, dawn', attested throughout Classical Chinese) with the noun-forming time/location suffix 上. Pairs with 好 to form the warm greeting 早上好！ ('Good morning!').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 早上 (via 萌典)

早晨.etymology: Coordinative temporal noun compound of 早 ('early morning') + 晨 ('daybreak, morning', sun 日 + 辰 'time of morning fieldwork'): 'morning, early morning'. Attested since the爾雅 Erya and Six Dynasties poetry.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 早晨 (via 萌典)

早间.etymology: Temporal compound noun and modifier of 早 ('early morning') + 间 (間, 'time interval, period'): 'in the morning, morning hours (e.g., 早间新闻 morning news)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 早间 (via 萌典)

早餐.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 早 ('morning') + 餐 ('meal'): 'breakfast' (slightly more formal or written than 早饭).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 早餐 (via 萌典)

早饭.etymology: Everyday compound noun of 早 ('morning') + 饭 (飯, 'cooked rice, meal'): 'breakfast'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 早饭 (via 萌典)

时.etymology: Ancient character (traditional 時) combining 日 ('sun') + 寺/之 (shí phonetic, originally a foot 止 stepping forward on the ground): 'the sun's movement through the year -> season (the four seasons 四时), time, hour (ancient double-hour 时辰 or modern o'clock), opportunity, when, from time to time'.

history.meaning: seasonal advance of the sun = season, time, hour

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 时 (via 萌典)

时候.etymology: Coordinative temporal noun compound pairing 时 (時, 'time, season') + 候 ('five-day micro-season or astronomical watch interval', neutral tone hou in this word). In Classical calendrical science, three 候 made one solar term (节气); in vernacular Mandarin 时候 fused into the general noun for 'time, moment, period, (when…的)时候'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 时候 (via 萌典)

时刻表.etymology: Three-character compound combining 时刻 ('hour and quarter-hour -> exact time') + 表 ('table, chart, schedule'): 'timetable, schedule (of trains, buses, flights, or classes)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 时刻表 (via 萌典)

时间.etymology: Compound noun of 时 (時, 'time') + 间 (間, 'interval, span'): 'time (both duration of time and a point in time)'.

history.meaning: span or point of time; time

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 时间 (via 萌典)

明亮.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 明 ('bright, luminous', sun 日 + moon 月 shining together) + 亮 ('bright, clear, shining'): 'bright, well-lit, luminous, shining'. Attested since Six Dynasties and Tang poetry.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 明亮 (via 萌典)

明信片.etymology: Three-character postal compound combining 明信 ('open/unsealed letter', 明 'open to view, unsealed' + 信 'letter') + 片 ('flat card, slip'): 'postcard' (introduced in late Qing postal service alongside Japanese 葉書).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 明信片 (via 萌典)

明天.etymology: Noun meaning 'tomorrow', combining 明 ('bright, next dawning', combining 日 'sun' + 月 'moon') with 天 ('day, sky'). Classical Chinese said 明日 ('next sun/day'); vernacular Mandarin replaced 日 with everyday 天 to form 明天.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 明天 (via 萌典)

明年.etymology: Temporal compound of 明 ('next, following', literally 'when the next cycle dawns into light') + 年 ('year'): 'next year'. Attested since the Zuozhuan and Analects.

history.stage: Classical Chinese (Zuozhuan, Analects) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 明年 (via 萌典)

明早.etymology: Contracted temporal compound of 明天 ('tomorrow', 明 'next') + 早晨/早上 ('morning'): 'tomorrow morning'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 明早 (via 萌典)

明明.etymology: Reduplication of 明 ('bright, clear, evident'). In the Classic of Poetry (Shijing) and Great Learning (明明德), 明明 meant 'illustrious and bright'; in vernacular Mandarin it functions as an epistemic/adversative adverb meaning 'obviously, plainly, clearly (contrary to what someone says or does)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 明明 (via 萌典)

明智.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 明 ('clear-sighted, discerning') + 智 ('wise, intelligent'): 'wise, sensible, sagacious'. Attested since the Hanshu and Three Kingdoms prose.

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 明智 (via 萌典)

星.etymology: Ancient character attested on Shang oracle bones originally showing three/five twinkling stars (晶) above phonetic 生 (shēng/xīng), later simplified to a single 日 ('celestial orb') above 生: 'star, heavenly body, planet, satellite; tiny speck/spark'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: celestial lights + phonetic 生 = star, heavenly body, speck

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 星 (via 萌典)

星期.etymology: Compound noun of 星 ('star/heavenly body') + 期 ('cycle, appointed period'). In Classical poetry (such as the Seventh Night festival of the Cowherd and Weaver Girl), 星期 meant 'the appointed tryst of the stars'. In the late Qing dynasty (promoted by Yuan Jiasan and early modern calendars to replace the older Seven Luminaries 七曜 cycle), 星期 was adopted for the seven-day 'week' (because the 7 days of the week were traditionally named after the Sun, Moon, and five visible planets).

history.stage: Late Qing to Modern Standard Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 星期 (via 萌典)

星期一.etymology: Calendar compound combining 星期 ('week') + 一 ('one, first day of the working week'): 'Monday'.

history.meaning: first day of the week = Monday

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 星期一 (via 萌典)

星期三.etymology: Calendar compound combining 星期 ('week') + 三 ('three, third day of the week'): 'Wednesday'.

history.meaning: third day of the week = Wednesday

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 星期三 (via 萌典)

星期二.etymology: Calendar compound combining 星期 ('week') + 二 ('two, second day of the week'): 'Tuesday'.

history.meaning: second day of the week = Tuesday

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 星期二 (via 萌典)

星期五.etymology: Calendar compound combining 星期 ('week') + 五 ('five, fifth day of the week'): 'Friday'.

history.meaning: fifth day of the week = Friday

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 星期五 (via 萌典)

星期六.etymology: Calendar compound combining 星期 ('week') + 六 ('six, sixth day of the week'): 'Saturday'.

history.meaning: sixth day of the week = Saturday

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 星期六 (via 萌典)

星期四.etymology: Calendar compound combining 星期 ('week') + 四 ('four, fourth day of the week'): 'Thursday'.

history.meaning: fourth day of the week = Thursday

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 星期四 (via 萌典)

星期天.etymology: Calendar compound combining 星期 ('week') + 天 ('day / Heaven', parallel to 星期日 and 礼拜天): 'Sunday'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 星期天 (via 萌典)

星级.etymology: Compound noun of 星 ('star') + 级 (級, 'grade, rating tier'): 'star rating (of hotels, restaurants, or service quality)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 星级 (via 萌典)

春天.etymology: Compound season noun of 春 ('spring', showing grass/plants 艸 sprouting under the warming sun 日 with phonetic 屯 chūn) + 天 ('season, sky, time of year'): 'spring, springtime'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 春天 (via 萌典)

昨天.etymology: Temporal compound of 昨 ('yesterday, the day just past', sun/day 日 + 乍 zhà) + 天 ('day'): 'yesterday'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 昨天 (via 萌典)

昨晚.etymology: Contracted temporal compound of 昨天 ('yesterday') + 晚上 ('evening, night'): 'last night, yesterday evening'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 昨晚 (via 萌典)

是.etymology: Equative copula ('be: am, is, are') linking two nouns or noun phrases. In Classical Chinese (Analects, Mencius), 是 originally functioned as the proximal demonstrative 'this' and adjective 'right, correct'; in Han-dynasty prose its résumé position between topic and predicate ('X, this [is] Y') reanalyzed into the modern copula 'be'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 是 (via 萌典)

是不是.etymology: A-not-A affirmative-negative question construction built on the copula 是 ('is') + 不 ('not') + 是 ('is'): literally 'is it or is it not?', used to form yes-no questions, tag questions ('…right?, isn't it?'), or express 'whether or not'.

history.meaning: is it or not?; right?; whether or not

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 是不是 (via 萌典)

显得.etymology: Evaluative verb-complement compound combining 显 (顯, 'show, appear, manifest visibly') + structural particle 得 (de): 'appear, seem, look (followed by an adjective or verb phrase, e.g., 显得很年轻 'look very young')'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 显得 (via 萌典)

晚.etymology: Phono-semantic character combining 日 ('sun/day') + 免 (miǎn/wǎn phonetic, 'draw away'): 'the sun drawing down at the end of the day -> evening, night; late (opposite of 早 'early'); junior/later'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 晚 (via 萌典)

晚上.etymology: Temporal noun combining 晚 ('evening, night') + nominal locative/temporal suffix 上 (neutral tone shang): 'in the evening, at night'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 晚上 (via 萌典)

晚安.etymology: Polite bedtime/parting greeting combining 晚 ('evening, night') + 安 ('peace, peaceful rest'): 'Good night!'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 晚安 (via 萌典)

晚茶.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 晚 ('evening; late-season') + 茶 ('tea'): 'evening tea (and dim sum snacks served in the evening); late-harvest tea'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 晚茶 (via 萌典)

晚饭.etymology: Everyday compound noun of 晚 ('evening') + 饭 (飯, 'cooked rice, meal'): 'dinner, supper, evening meal'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 晚饭 (via 萌典)

晴天.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 晴 ('clear, cloudless sky after rain', sun 日 + 青 'clear blue') + 天 ('sky, day, weather'): 'sunny day, clear day, fair weather'. Attested since Tang poetry.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 晴天 (via 萌典)

晴朗.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 晴 ('clear and sunny', sun 日 + 青) + 朗 ('bright and clear', 良 + 月 'bright moonlight'): '(of the sky or weather) clear and bright, sunny and cloudless'.

history.stage: Classical & Tang–Song Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 晴朗 (via 萌典)

暖.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 日 ('warming sun', historically also written 煖 with 火 'fire') + 爰 (yuán/nuǎn phonetic): 'warm, genial (of weather, sunlight, or feelings); warm up'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese (Mencius, Chuci) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: warm (from fire or sun); warm up

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 暖 (via 萌典)

暖和.etymology: Coordinative adjective and verb compound of 暖 ('warm') + 和 ('mild, gentle', pronounced neutral tone huo in this word): 'nice and warm, pleasantly warm; warm up'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 暖和 (via 萌典)

暖暖.etymology: Vivid AA-reduplication of the adjective 暖 ('warm'): 'cosily warm, softly warm' (first attested in Laozi's 暧暧内含光 / 暖暖).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 暖暖 (via 萌典)

暗.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 日 ('sun/light') + 音 (yīn/àn phonetic): 'lack of sunlight -> dark, dim, gloomy (opposite of 明/亮); hidden, secret, in the dark'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 暗 (via 萌典)

暗门.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 暗 ('hidden, concealed, secret') + 门 (門, 'door'): 'hidden door, secret door, concealed doorway set flush with a wall'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 暗门 (via 萌典)

暴风雨.etymology: Three-character weather compound combining 暴 ('sudden, fierce, violent', 日 'scorching sun' + 出 + 廾 + 米) + 风雨 ('wind and rain'): 'rainstorm, tempest, storm' (both meteorological and figurative).

history.meaning: violent wind and rain; rainstorm; tempest

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 暴风雨 (via 萌典)

曲子.etymology: Colloquial noun formed from 曲 (read qǔ in the third tone, 'melody, tune, song, verse lyric', extended from 曲 qū 'bent, winding' -> 'winding melodic turns of a tune') + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): 'tune, melody, piece of music'.

history.stage: Tang–Song–Yuan music & drama to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 曲子 (via 萌典)

更.etymology: Ancient character combining 丙 + 攵 ('strike/alter'): read gēng as a verb/noun meaning 'change, replace, alternate; night-watch period (one of the five two-hour night watches 五更 struck on a drum/gong)'; read gèng as Mandarin's primary comparative degree adverb meaning 'even more, still more, further'.

history.meaning: change, alternate, night watch (gēng); even more, further (gèng)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 更 (via 萌典)

替.etymology: Ideogram combining two standing figures (夫/立) side by side above 日/曰: originally 'one replacing or supplanting another', hence the verb 'replace, substitute for, take the place of' and the benefactive preposition 'for, on behalf of'.

history.meaning: take the place of; for / on behalf of

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 替 (via 萌典)

最.etymology: Ideogram combining 曰/冃 ('cap/cover') + 取 ('take by the ear, seize first prize in battle'): originally 'take the foremost/top share', grammaticalized since Han texts into Chinese's primary superlative degree adverb 'most, -est'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 最 (via 萌典)

最后.etymology: Superlative temporal/spatial noun and adjective combining 最 ('most, -est') + 后 (後, 'after, behind, last'): 'the very last, final; finally, in the end, at last'.

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese (Shiji) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 最后 (via 萌典)

最多.etymology: Superlative quantifier and adverb combining 最 ('most') + 多 ('many, much'): 'the most (in quantity); at most, at the outside'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 最多 (via 萌典)

月.etymology: Foundational pictograph (象形字) attested from Shang oracle bones depicting a crescent moon: 'the moon; month (originally the lunar synodic month of ~29.5 days, now each of the 12 calendar months); monthly'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 月 (via 萌典)

月底.etymology: Temporal compound of 月 ('month') + 底 ('bottom, end'): 'the end of the month'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 月底 (via 萌典)

有.etymology: Verb of possession ('have') and existence ('there is, there are'), attested from Shang oracle bones and bronze inscriptions through Classical and modern Mandarin. Unlike every other Mandarin verb, 有 is always negated with 没 (没有), never 不.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 有 (via 萌典)

有力.etymology: Verb-object compound used as an adjective, combining 有 ('have, possess') + 力 ('strength, force, power'): 'strong, forceful, powerful, vigorous'. Attested since the Shijing.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 有力 (via 萌典)

有时候.etymology: Temporal phrase combining 有 ('there are') + 时候 ('times, occasions'): 'there are times when… -> sometimes, at times, now and then'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 有时候 (via 萌典)

有点.etymology: Degree adverb and quantifier phrase contracted from 有一点 ('have a little bit of'): before adjectives or psychological verbs (有点累, 有点冷) it serves as a degree adverb meaning 'somewhat, a bit, rather'; before nouns it means 'have a little (of something)'.

morphemes.meaning: a little bit (short for 一点)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 有点 (via 萌典)

朋友.etymology: Coordinative noun compound pairing two ancient relationship terms: 朋 (originally two strings of cowrie shells 玨 hung together -> 'fellow students who study under the same master') + 友 (two right hands 又 joined in mutual assistance -> 'comrades who share the same aspirations', neutral tone you in modern speech): 'friend'. Famously in the opening line of the Analects: 有朋自远方来，不亦乐乎.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones, Shijing, Analects) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: fellow students (朋) and helpful comrades (友) -> friend

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 朋友 (via 萌典)

服务.etymology: Verb-object/coordinative compound of 服 ('submit to, undertake duties, serve') + 务 (務, 'devote effort to, task, business'): 'serve, provide service; service'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 服务 (via 萌典)

朝.etymology: Ancient character attested on Shang oracle bones showing the sun (日) rising among grass/trees (茻) while the pale moon/tide (月/舟) is still visible: read zhāo 'morning, dawn, day'; extended to morning royal audiences at court and read cháo 'imperial court, dynasty; face toward, look toward; preposition toward'.

history.meaning: morning dawn (zhāo); attend morning court, dynasty, face toward (cháo)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 朝 (via 萌典)

木.etymology: Foundational pictograph (象形字) attested from Shang oracle bones depicting a tree with branches above and roots below the ground line: 'tree (in Classical Chinese); wood, timber, lumber; wooden; numb/stiff'.

history.meaning: pictograph of a tree with crown and roots = tree, wood

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 木 (via 萌典)

木匠.etymology: Compound occupational noun of 木 ('wood') + 匠 ('artisan, craftsman', showing an axe 斤 inside a tool box 匚, neutral tone jiang in everyday speech): 'carpenter, joiner, woodworker'. Attested since Han–Tang prose.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 木匠 (via 萌典)

木头.etymology: Colloquial noun formed from 木 ('wood, tree') + nominal suffix 头 (頭, neutral tone tou, originally denoting a block/end of cut timber): 'wood, log, timber, piece of wood'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 木头 (via 萌典)

木工.etymology: Compound noun of 木 ('wood') + 工 ('craftwork, artisan'): means both 'woodworking, carpentry' and 'carpenter, woodworker'. Attested since the Book of Rites (Liji: 考工记).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 木工 (via 萌典)

木工房.etymology: Three-character compound combining 木工 ('woodworking, carpentry') + 房 ('room, workshop'): 'woodworking shop, carpentry workshop'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 木工房 (via 萌典)

木桌.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 木 ('wooden') + 桌 ('table, desk'): 'wooden table'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 木桌 (via 萌典)

木窗.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 木 ('wooden') + 窗 ('window'): 'wooden-framed window, wooden window'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 木窗 (via 萌典)

木箱.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 木 ('wooden') + 箱 ('box, chest, crate'): 'wooden box, wooden chest or crate'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 木箱 (via 萌典)

木花架.etymology: Three-character compound combining 木 ('wooden') + 花架 ('flower stand, plant rack'): 'wooden flower stand, wooden plant shelf'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 木花架 (via 萌典)

木门.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 木 ('wooden') + 门 (門, 'door'): 'wooden door'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 木门 (via 萌典)

本.etymology: Measure word for bound books, notebooks, and ledgers (一本书 'a book', 一本账本 'a ledger'). Formed by marking the lower root of 木 ('tree') with a stroke, 本 meant 'tree root, foundation, origin' in Classical Chinese, then 'bound volume' once bamboo slips were superseded by stitched codices.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 本 (via 萌典)

本地.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun and modifier of 本 ('root -> this, current, native') + 地 ('place, locality'): 'this locality, local, native'. Attested since Song–Ming texts.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 本地 (via 萌典)

本子.etymology: Colloquial noun formed from 本 (indicative character showing a mark 一 at the root of a tree 木: 'root, source -> bound volume, edition, notebook') + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): 'notebook, exercise book, pad, bound booklet'.

history.stage: Song–Ming book printing to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 本子 (via 萌典)

本来.etymology: Compound adjective and adverb of 本 ('root, origin, original') + 来 ('come from the beginning'). Originated in Medieval Buddhist translations and Tang–Song prose for 'original nature', and in Mandarin means 'original, originally; of course, as a matter of fact'.

history.stage: Tang–Song Buddhist & vernacular Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 本来 (via 萌典)

机油.etymology: Compound noun of 机 (機, 'machine, engine', shortened from 机器) + 油 ('oil, lubricant'): 'engine oil, motor oil, machine lubricating oil'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 机油 (via 萌典)

杏仁.etymology: Compound of 杏 ('apricot/almond tree', wood 木 + 口) + 仁 ('edible seed kernel inside a pit', extended from 'humane heart/core' to the tender inner seed of stone fruits); used in Chinese baking and herbal cuisine for sweet almonds and apricot kernels.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 杏仁

条.etymology: Measure word for long, narrow, or winding things: streets, lanes, rivers, towels, trousers, and legal clauses (一条老街 'an old street', 一条毛巾 'a towel'). In the Classic of Poetry, 條 originally named a long, slender tree branch, from which the long-strip classifier grew.

history.meaning: classifier for streets, rivers, ropes, clauses

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 條 (via 萌典)

条例.etymology: Coordinative legal noun compound of 条 (條, 'branch -> numbered article or clause of a code') + 例 ('precedent, rule, regulation'): 'regulations, ordinances, bylaws, statutory rules'. Attested since Tang–Song administrative law.

history.stage: Tang–Song administrative law to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 条例 (via 萌典)

条文.etymology: Compound legal noun of 条 (條, 'numbered clause, article') + 文 ('written text, wording'): 'written clauses or provisions (of a law, contract, or regulation)'.

history.stage: Tang–Song legal Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: written articles or clauses of a law/contract

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 条文 (via 萌典)

来.etymology: Pictograph (來) in Shang oracle-bone script of a ripening wheat plant (麦) with awns, ears, and roots. Because wheat was traditionally seen as aheaven-sent grain that 'came' from afar, 來 was borrowed from the earliest inscriptions for the verb 'come (toward the speaker), arrive; next/future (来年); do (a colloquial pro-verb); approximate number suffix (十来个); since (三天来)'.

history.meaning: wheat plant graph borrowed for 'come, arrive'
come; arrive; pro-verb; directional complement toward speaker

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 来 (via 萌典)

来不及.etymology: Potential verb-complement compound combining 来 ('come, make it in time') + 不 ('not') + 及 ('reach, catch up with in time'): 'there's not enough time (to do something), too late to'.

history.meaning: cannot make it in time; too late

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 来不及 (via 萌典)

来信.etymology: Modifier-head / verb-object compound of 来 ('come toward the recipient, incoming') + 信 ('letter'): 'incoming letter, your letter; send a letter here'.

history.stage: Tang–Song epistolary Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 来信 (via 萌典)

来回.etymology: Antonymic directional compound pairing 来 ('come') + 回 ('return, go back'): 'go back and forth, round trip; a round trip (as a noun/classifier)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 来回 (via 萌典)

杯.etymology: Noun 'cup' and measure word for cupfuls or glassfuls of drinks (一杯热茶 'a cup of hot tea', 一杯咖啡 'a cup of coffee'). Written with 木 ('wood', reflecting early lacquered wooden drinking vessels) and 不 phonetic, 杯 is attested in Classical banqueting scenes in the Shiji and Mencius.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 杯 (via 萌典)

杯子.etymology: Formed from 杯 ('cup', phono-semantic character with 木 'wood'—reflecting early lacquered wooden drinking vessels—and phonetic 不) plus the nominalizing diminutive suffix 子 (neutral tone zi), which turns monosyllabic nouns into natural two-syllable spoken Mandarin words.

history.meaning: lacquered wooden or ceramic wine/soup cup

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 杯子 (via 萌典)

松.etymology: Merged simplified graph representing two historical characters: (1) 松 (wood 木 + 公 gōng/sōng phonetic: 'pine tree', symbol of longevity and resilience in Chinese culture) and (2) 鬆 (hair 髟 + 松 sōng phonetic: 'loose, disheveled hair -> loose, slack, relax, loosen, soft and flaky').

history.form: 松 (pine tree) / 鬆 (loose, slack, relax)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 松 (via 萌典)

极了.etymology: Post-adjectival degree intensifier combining 极 (極, 'ridgepole of a roof -> utmost point, extreme') + modal particle 了 (le): placed directly after an adjective or psychological verb (好极了 'wonderful!', 高兴极了 'extremely happy') to mean 'extremely, to the utmost'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 极了 (via 萌典)

枕头.etymology: Colloquial noun formed from 枕 ('wooden headrest/pillow', wood 木 + 冘 yín, because ancient Chinese pillows were carved from wood, bamboo, or porcelain before cloth/filled pillows) + nominal suffix 头 (頭, neutral tone tou): 'pillow'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 枕头 (via 萌典)

果酱.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 果 ('fruit') + 酱 (醬, 'thick fermented or cooked paste/sauce'): 'jam, fruit preserves, marmalade'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 果酱 (via 萌典)

枝条.etymology: Coordinative botanical noun compound pairing 枝 ('tree branch', wood 木 + 支) + 条 (條, 'slender twig, shoot'): 'branches and twigs, slender boughs'. Attested since the漢書 Book of Han and Six Dynasties poetry.

history.stage: Han–Six Dynasties Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 枝条 (via 萌典)

架.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 加 (jiā, 'place one atop another') + 木 ('wood'): 'wooden frame, rack, stand, shelf, trestle; prop up, support; quarrel/fight (吵架, 打架); classifier for framed machines, aircraft, pianos, or cameras (一架飞机, 一架钢琴)'.

history.meaning: shelf/frame; prop up; classifier for planes, pianos, machines

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 架 (via 萌典)

架子.etymology: Colloquial noun formed from 架 ('wooden frame, stand, rack') + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): means literally 'shelf, rack, stand, framework' and figuratively 'haughty airs, pretension (摆架子 put on airs)'.

history.meaning: shelf; rack; stand; framework; haughty airs

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 架子 (via 萌典)

柔化.etymology: Derived causative verb combining 柔 ('soft, gentle, supple', 矛 + 木 'pliable wood') + verbalizing suffix 化 ('transform into, -ize, -en'): 'soften (light, edges, tone, or contrast), make gentle'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 柔化 (via 萌典)

柔和.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 柔 ('soft, supple, gentle') + 和 ('mild, gentle, harmonious'): 'soft, gentle, mild (of light, colors, music, voice, or breeze)'. Attested since Classical prose and poetry.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 柔和 (via 萌典)

柜台.etymology: Compound noun of 柜 (櫃, 'cabinet, chest') + 台 (臺, 'raised counter, platform'): 'shop counter, service desk/counter (in a store, hotel, bank, or airport)'.

history.stage: Ming–Qing commercial vernacular to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 柜台 (via 萌典)

柜子.etymology: Colloquial noun formed from 柜 (櫃, combining 木 'wood' + 巨/匱 guì: 'wooden storage cabinet or chest') + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): 'cabinet, cupboard, wardrobe, chest'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 柜子 (via 萌典)

柠檬.etymology: Disyllabic phonetic loan for 'lemon' written with two tree-radical characters (木 + 宁 níng and 木 + 蒙 méng). Attested in Song–Yuan maritime and botanical records (such as Fan Chengda's Guihai Yuheng Zhi and southern trade glossaries) transcribing Indo-Iranian / Malay-Arabic citrus terms ultimately akin to Sanskrit nimbū and Persian līmūn.

morphemes.kind: phonetic loan syllable (with 木 tree radical)
phonetic loan syllable (with 木 tree radical)

history.meaning: tart citrus fruit cultivated in Lingnan

cognates.meaning: citrus fruit borrowed along the same Indo-Persian trade network

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 柠檬 (via 萌典)

柠檬塔.etymology: Three-character culinary compound combining 柠檬 ('lemon', a phonetic loan via Cantonese/Southeast Asian trade from Persian/Arabic līmūn / English lemon, written with the tree radical 木) + 塔 ('tart', phonetic loan from French tarte / English tart): 'lemon tart'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 柠檬塔 (via 萌典)

柠檬挞.etymology: Three-character culinary compound combining 柠檬 ('lemon') + 挞 (撻, tà, phonetic transcription of 'tart'): 'lemon tart' (orthographic variant of 柠檬塔 using 挞 specifically for Western pastry tarts).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 柠檬挞 (via 萌典)

标题.etymology: Coordinative noun compound of 标 (標, 'treetop mark, signpost, label') + 题 (題, 'forehead -> inscription, title, heading'): 'title, heading, headline, caption'.

history.stage: Tang–Song literary & administrative Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 标题 (via 萌典)

栋.etymology: Phono-semantic character (棟) of 木 ('wood/tree') + 东 (東, dōng/dòng phonetic): in Classical architecture 'the main central ridgepole of a building' (preserved in 栋梁 'ridgepole and beam -> pillar of the state'). Because counting ridgepoles counted whole buildings, it became the standard classifier for 'a building, house, or apartment block (一栋楼)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 栋 (via 萌典)

树.etymology: Phono-semantic/ideographic character (traditional 樹, combining 木 'tree' + 尌 shù 'stand a drum upright with the hand'). In Classical Chinese, 'tree' as a noun was 木, while 樹 was the verb 'plant (trees), set up upright' (as in 百年树人). From the Six Dynasties and Tang period onward, 樹 replaced 木 as the everyday noun for a living 'tree'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 树 (via 萌典)

树下.etymology: Locative compound combining 树 ('tree') + 下 ('under, beneath'): 'under the tree, beneath the trees'.

history.stage: Six Dynasties–Tang poetry to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 树下 (via 萌典)

树叶.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 树 ('tree') + 叶 (葉, 'leaf of a plant', originally depicting flat leaves growing on a tree 木, before葉 added the grass radical 艹 and simplified back to 叶): 'tree leaf, leaves, foliage'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 树叶 (via 萌典)

核桃木.etymology: Three-character timber compound combining 核桃 ('walnut', originally 胡桃 'Central Asian peach/nut' introduced along the Silk Road during the Han dynasty, later written 核桃 'kernel peach') + 木 ('wood, timber'): 'walnut wood'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 核桃木 (via 萌典)

根.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 木 ('tree') + 艮 (gèn/gēn phonetic): 'root of a tree or plant; base, foot, foundation, cause/origin' and the standard classifier for long, slender objects (strings, wires, hairs, pillars, bananas, matches: 一根线).

history.meaning: root of a tree or plant; foundation
root; base; classifier for long slender objects

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 根 (via 萌典)

根本.etymology: Coordinative noun, adjective, and adverb compound pairing two Classical 'tree-root' words: 根 ('root') + 本 ('base/root of a trunk'). Means 'root, foundation, fundamental/essential', and before negatives (根本不/没) an emphatic adverb meaning 'at all, simply, from the ground up'.

history.meaning: roots and trunk base -> foundation, fundamental
fundamental; root; (with negation) at all, simply

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 根本 (via 萌典)

桌.etymology: Phono-semantic/ideographic character combining 卓 (zhuō, 'tall, elevated upright') + 木 ('wood'): 'high wooden table'. Emerged during the Tang–Song transition when high-legged tables and chairs (桌椅) replaced ancient low floor-sitting mats and low tables (几案).

history.stage: Tang–Song furniture evolution to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 桌 (via 萌典)

桌子.etymology: Colloquial noun formed from 桌 ('high wooden table') + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): 'table, desk'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 桌子 (via 萌典)

桌布.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 桌 ('table') + 布 ('cloth'): 'tablecloth'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 桌布 (via 萌典)

桥.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 橋) of 木 ('wood', as early bridges were timber structures) + 乔 (喬, qiáo, 'tall and arched'): 'bridge'. Attested since the Shijing and Mencius.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 桥 (via 萌典)

桩.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 樁) of 木 ('wood') + 庄 (莊, zhuāng phonetic): 'wooden stake, post, or pile driven into the ground' and a classifier for matters, cases, or transactions (一桩事 'a matter').

history.meaning: wooden stake/pile; classifier for matters or deals

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 桩 (via 萌典)

桶.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 木 ('wood', from staved wooden pails) + 甬 (yǒng/tǒng, 'tubular vessel/measure'): 'bucket, pail, barrel, tub, bin' and classifier for buckets or barrels.

history.meaning: wooden bucket, pail, barrel, or tub

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 桶 (via 萌典)

梦寐以求.etymology: Four-character Classical idiom combining 梦寐 ('in dreams and sleep', 梦 'dream' + 寐 'sleep', echoing the opening ode of the Shijing: 窈窕淑女，寤寐求之 'waking and sleeping he sought her') + 以 ('therein / wherewith') + 求 ('seek'): 'long for even in one's dreams, crave/dream of attaining'.

history.stage: Classical Chinese (modeled on Shijing's 寤寐求之) to Modern Mandarin
history.form: 夢寐以求 / 梦寐以求
history.meaning: seek even in one's dreams; long-dreamed-of

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 梦寐以求 (via 萌典)

梦想.etymology: Modifier-head verb and noun compound of 梦 (夢, 'dream') + 想 ('think of, long for, aspiration'): originally 'think of in a dream, vain daydream' in Song prose, and in modern Mandarin 'cherished dream, aspiration; dream of'.

history.stage: Song dynasty prose to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: dream of; cherished dream or aspiration

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 梦想 (via 萌典)

梧桐巷.etymology: Three-character street name combining 梧桐 ('Chinese parasol tree, Firmiana simplex', a poetic shade tree famous in Chinese literature and lane plantings) + 巷 ('lane, alley'): 'Wutong Lane (Parasol-Tree Alley)'.

history.meaning: Wutong Lane (lane lined with Chinese parasol trees)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 梧桐巷 (via 萌典)

梯子.etymology: Derived from 梯 ('wooden steps or ladder', wood radical 木 + phonetic 弟 dì, which also carries the sense 'ordered sequence/steps') + nominal suffix 子 (-zi).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 梯子

检查.etymology: Coordinative verb and noun compound of 检 (檢, 'inspect, verify, restrain') + 查 ('examine, investigate, look into'): 'inspect, check, examine; self-criticism/inspection'.

history.stage: Tang–Song administrative Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 检查 (via 萌典)

棒.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 木 ('wood') + 奉 (fèng/bàng phonetic): originally 'wooden club, stick, cudgel, baton'. In northern Mandarin vernacular, from 'sturdy/solid like a heavy stick', it developed the lively adjective sense 'great, awesome, excellent, strong, capable (真棒!)'.

history.stage: Qing northern vernacular to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 棒 (via 萌典)

棕色.etymology: Modifier-head color compound of 棕 ('coir palm fiber', stripped from the trunk of the windmill palm 棕榈, naturally dark reddish-brown) + 色 ('color'): 'brown'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 棕色 (via 萌典)

椅.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 木 ('wood') + 奇 (qí/yǐ phonetic). In the Shijing, 椅 (read yī) named a catalpa-like tree; during the Tang–Song adoption of high-backed seating (originally called 绳床 or 倚床, from 倚 yǐ 'lean one's back against'), 椅 (read yǐ) was repurposed for a 'chair with a backrest'.

history.stage: Tang–Song furniture evolution to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 椅 (via 萌典)

椅子.etymology: Formed from 椅 (wood radical 木 + phonetic 奇 qí; originally a type of catalpa tree in Classical texts, reassigned during the Tang–Song transition from floor mats to high-seated backed chairs) + nominal suffix 子.

history.meaning: folding chair and backed wooden chair

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 椅子 (via 萌典)

楼.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 樓) of 木 ('wood/timber construction') + 娄 (婁, lóu, whose stacked components also evoke multiple stories piled up): 'multi-story building, tower, upper floor/story (二楼 second floor)'.

history.meaning: multi-story timber building; watchtower; upper floor

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 楼 (via 萌典)

楼上.etymology: Locative compound combining 楼 ('storied building, floor') + 上 ('up, above'): 'upstairs, on an upper floor'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 楼上 (via 萌典)

楼下.etymology: Locative compound combining 楼 ('storied building, floor') + 下 ('down, below'): 'downstairs, below the building'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 楼下 (via 萌典)

楼梯.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 楼 ('multi-story building, upper floor') + 梯 ('wooden ladder, steps', 木 + 弟 'sequential steps'): 'stairs, staircase, stairway'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 楼梯 (via 萌典)

楼梯口.etymology: Three-character locative compound combining 楼梯 ('staircase, stairs') + 口 ('opening, entrance'): 'stairway entrance, head or foot of the stairs, landing'.

history.meaning: head or foot of the stairs; stairwell entrance

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 楼梯口 (via 萌典)

橄榄油.etymology: Compound of 橄榄 ('olive', originally naming native Chinese Canarium white/black olives with wood radical 木 on both characters, then applied to Mediterranean Olea europaea) + 油 ('pressed oil').
